designed by the Aelindra team.<br> Built with Twine / SugarCube 2.</p> <p class="nav-return"><<link "◄ Back to Title" "title-screen">><</link>></p> </div>/* ============================================================ DAY 0 ("The Rite") — SCENE & NPC FLAG INIT Called once, from day-1_sleep_transition.tw, mirroring day-1-init.tw / day-2-init.tw. Opens with <<clearObjectives>> per the established convention (see day-1-init.tw for the full rationale). ARCHITECTURE NOTE: Day 0 is split. The morning (day0_wake -> day0_hub and its sub-hubs) is open-world, same as every previous day. But entering day0_bridge is a hard point of no return — day0_hub is never linked back to after that, and the game becomes fully linear: bridge -> path choice -> ritual (female or futa, permanently divergent) -> void -> Day 1 (day1_hub, or the new day1_hub_futa). $gamePath, set at the path choice, is what a body of future Day 1+ content keys off of to know which branch it's in. ============================================================ */ <<widget "day0Init">> <<clearObjectives>> /* --- Day 0 Scene Flags --- */ <<set $d0_wake to false>> <<set $d0_queens_gift to false>> <<set $d0_queen to false>> <<set $d0_bridge to false>> <<set $d0_pathChosen to false>> <<set $d0_ritual to false>> <<set $d0_void to false>> /* --- Day 0 NPC / side-content Flags --- */ <<set $d0_npc_brin to false>> <<set $d0_npc_sword to false>> <<set $d0_npc_caedric to false>> <<set $d0_npc_maids2 to false>> <<set $d0_npc_aldric_gift to false>> <<set $d0_npc_marta3 to false>> <<set $d0_npc_haeth to false>> <<set $d0_npc_wynn3 to false>> <<set $d0_npc_alva3 to false>> <<set $d0_npc_nara2 to false>> <<set $d0_npc_vael2 to false>> <<set $d0_npc_morningwood to false>> <<set $d0_npc_watching to false>> /* --- Items collected this day --- */ <<set $hasAldricSword to false>> <<set $hasAldricLetter to false>> <<set $hasMoonflower to false>> <<set $hasJasmine to false>> <<set $hasGingerRoot to false>> <<set $hasHandkerchief to false>> /* --- Point of no return --- */ <<set $bridgeWarningAcknowledged to false>> /* --- Day framing --- */ <<set $dayNumber to 0>> <<set $dayLabel to "The Rite">> <<set $timeSlot to "MORNING">> /* --- Objectives --- Queen's Gift is listed first per its own integration note: Seraphina timed it to arrive before the goodbye, pleasure before grief before the tower. The bridge objective is added now and stays visible the whole morning, carrying its own warning text baked into the hub card rather than a separate objective-panel warning. */ <<addObjective "queens_gift" "A knock at the door — not a servant's" "MAIN">> <<addObjective "farewell_queen" "Say goodbye — the Queen's Chambers" "MAIN">> <<addObjective "cross_bridge" "When you're ready — cross the bridge to the Moonspire Tower" "MAIN">> <</widget>><div class="scene-image"><<locationImage "moonspire_bridge" "The Bridge">></div> <h2>The Bridge — Crossing</h2> <p>The covered bridge stretches between the palace and the Moonspire Tower like a stone throat connecting two worlds. Thirty paces long. Open on both sides to the wind that howls through the chasm, carrying spray from the river far below — a sound like the world clearing its throat, like the earth coughing up its own deep water.</p> <p>I step onto the bridge.</p> <p>Rowan is there.</p> <p><<npcPortrait "rowan" "Rowan">>They're leaning against the railing at the near end, lute absent for the first time I can remember. Their arms are crossed. Their honey-coloured eyes find mine immediately — they've been waiting. They said they would be. <em>I'll be in the courtyard. Before dawn. If you walk toward the tower, I'll walk with you.</em></p> <p>They don't say anything. They push off the railing and fall into step beside me. Their shoulder brushes mine. The contact is deliberate and grounding — a tether, a reminder that the body walking this bridge is real and solid and present, not yet dissolved into the thing it's about to become.</p> <p>We walk. The wind roars. The spray catches my face — cold, sharp, tasting of minerals and deep earth. Below, the river carves through the gorge with the patient violence of water that has been doing this for a thousand years and will continue for a thousand more, indifferent to the small human drama crossing above it.</p> <p>Halfway across, I stop. My hands find the stone railing. The stone is worn smooth — centuries of hands gripping this rail, centuries of people crossing between the mundane world and the magical one, bringing their fears and their desperation and their impossible hopes to the tower that glows faintly white against the morning sky.</p> <p>I look down. Not suicidal. Not considering it. Just... the vertigo. The dizziness of standing between who I am and who I'm about to become, with nothing below but a long fall and cold water and the implacable fact of gravity.</p> <p>Rowan stands beside me. Looking down too. Their hair catches the wind — dark with copper, whipping across their face.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"You don't have to watch me go in," I say.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ROWAN</span>"I know."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Then why are you here?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ROWAN</span>"Because that's what friends do. They walk you to the places you're afraid to go, and they wait outside, and they're there when you come out the other side."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"What if what comes out isn't me?"</div> <p>Rowan turns. Looks at me. Their expression is something I've never seen on them before — not the easy warmth, not the performer's charm, not the gentle deflection of someone who's learned to keep the world at arm's length with humour and music. Something raw. Something that costs them.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ROWAN</span>"It'll be you. Different wrapping. Same person. I'll know you. I've always known you."</div> <p>They put their hand on my arm. The grip is firm. Lute-calloused fingers pressing through the leather of my jerkin, and I can feel the warmth of their palm and the slight tremor that tells me they're not as calm as they're performing and that undoes me more than anything else today — the knowledge that Rowan, who is never shaken, is shaking.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ROWAN</span>"Go. I'll be right here. Right here on this bridge. When you wake up."</div> <p>I nod. I can't speak. My throat has closed around every word I could possibly say and sealed them in like a tomb.</p> <p>I walk the remaining fifteen paces. The tower entrance looms — white stone, arched doorway, carved symbols that pulse faintly silver. Ilara is there.</p> <p><<npcPortrait "ilara" "Archsorceress Ilara">>She's wearing the full ceremonial robes of the Silverveil — deep purple, silver-threaded, a crescent moon pendant at her throat that catches the morning light. Behind her, four sorceresses stand in a line — hooded, robed, silent, radiating that electric-ozone pressure of concentrated magic. The air around them hums.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I'm not choosing this." My voice comes out steady. I don't know how. "I'm choosing the thing that isn't watching everything my mother built be destroyed."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"That's still a choice."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"It's the worst one I've ever made."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"Not the worst. The hardest. There's a difference."</div> <p>I look up at the tower. White stone rising into a sky that's beginning to show the first pale colours of morning — lavender, dove-grey, the faintest blush of gold at the eastern horizon. The tower doesn't care about my feelings. It's been here for centuries, performing its function, remaking the world one body at a time.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Will it hurt?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"Yes."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Good. I want to remember I didn't go willingly."</div> <p>I climb the stairs. Behind me, I hear Rowan's lute — they've produced it from somewhere, as they always do, and the first notes drift up the stairwell like a benediction. Something without words. Something that says <em>I'm here, I'm here, I'm here.</em></p> <p>The stairs spiral upward. The tapestries shift as I pass — the serpent becoming the river, the tree becoming the woman, the bird becoming the song. I've seen them before. Today they feel like prophecy.</p> <<set $d0_bridge to true>> <<set $timeSlot to "MIDDAY">> <<set $mcPortrait to "edrin_default">> <<clearObjectives>> <div class="scene-end"> <<if $gamePath is "none">> [[Continue → |day0_path_choice]] <<elseif $gamePath is "female">> [[Continue → |day0_ritual_female]] <<else>> [[Continue → |day0_ritual_futa]] <</if>> </div><div class="bridge-confirm"> <h2>⚠ Point of No Return</h2> <p>Once you cross the bridge, the Rite will begin. Especially now.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Brin."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">BRIN</span>"Your Highness?"</div> <p>I look at him. Sixteen. Sandy hair. Too-big livery. A boy from the tanner's family in the Lower Market who got a palace job because the crown offers patronage to common families. He's been bringing my breakfast for three weeks. He knows how I take my bread — stale, if possible. He knows I eat standing at the window. He remembers the pastry compliment and relayed it to Marta and it made her day.</p> <p>In three days, a woman will be sitting in this room. Brin will bring her breakfast. He'll be confused. He'll adapt — servants always adapt, it's the job — but the prince he's been learning to serve will be gone, replaced by a princess he doesn't know, and the small, specific intimacy of remembering someone's breakfast preferences will have to be rebuilt from scratch.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Thank you," I say. It comes out weighted — too much meaning for two words, too much goodbye for a boy who doesn't know it's a goodbye.</div> <p>He blinks.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">BRIN</span>"You're welcome, Your Highness. Are you... is everything alright?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Everything's fine. The pastries are perfect."</div> <p>He smiles. He leaves. The door closes. The pastries are, in fact, perfect. I eat two of them standing at the window, looking down at the courtyard, and the cheese is hot and the rosemary is sharp and the last breakfast I eat as a man tastes like a childhood I didn't appreciate until it was over.</p> <<set $d0_npc_brin to true>> <<set $energy += 10>> <<set $stress -= 3>> <<set $repStaff += 1>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day0_chambers]] </div><<npcPortrait "caedric" "Ser Caedric">> <h3>Ser Caedric — The Bench, One Last Time</h3> <p>He's on the bench. Of course he's on the bench. The bench is as much a part of Caedric as the rusted sword at his hip. I don't know what the palace would do without Ser Caedric on this bench — it would be like removing a load-bearing wall.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"Prince Edrin." He doesn't stand. We stopped pretending years ago. "Early morning for you."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Couldn't sleep."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"You haven't slept properly in three days. I can tell by the depth of the circles under your eyes. Day one: mild shadow. Day two: noticeable. Today: architectural."</div> <p>I sit beside him. The bench is warm — body heat, accumulated over what must be hours. Caedric arrives before dawn and stays until after dusk. It's not laziness. It's commitment. He's chosen his post and he holds it.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"You're going to the tower today." Not a question. Caedric deals in certainties.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"How—"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"I'm seventy-three years old and I've been sitting on this bench watching this palace for twelve years. Ilara crossed the bridge at dawn in full ceremonial robes. The Queen's door has been closed since first light — no visitors, no ministers. The kitchen is running on crisis pastries. And you, Prince Edrin, are walking the corridors at an hour when you're usually still in bed, with the face of a man who is about to do something terrible and irreversible."</div> <p>He adjusts his sword belt. The leather creaks.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"I served your grandmother. Did I tell you that?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Several times."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"Then I'll tell you again, because old men repeat themselves and young princes humor them. Your grandmother took the throne at nineteen. She wasn't ready. She was terrified. She told me once — years later, when we were both old enough for honesty — that on coronation day, she looked in the mirror and saw a girl playing dress-up in her mother's crown. She felt like a fraud for the first five years."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"When did she stop?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"She didn't. She just got better at ruling while feeling like a fraud. That's the secret, Your Highness. Nobody ever feels ready. Not for the crown, not for the throne, not for..." He pauses. Looks at me. Those bright old eyes seeing everything, as always. "Not for any of it. You just do it, and the doing becomes the being, and one morning you wake up and the person in the mirror isn't a fraud anymore — she's just you."</div> <p><em>She.</em> He said <em>she.</em> Deliberately. Knowingly. This old knight on his bench, with his rusted sword and his institutional memory, knows exactly what I'm walking toward this morning, and he's already adjusted his pronouns.</p> <p>Something in my chest cracks. Just a little.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Ser Caedric."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"Your Highness."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Thank you. For the bench. For all of it."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"I'll be here." He settles back. Crosses his ankles. "I'm always here. That's the stubbornness."</div> <<set $d0_npc_caedric to true>> <<set $statRES += 3>> <<set $stress -= 8>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day0_corridors]] </div><<npcPortrait "haeth" "Haeth">> <h3>Haeth — The Book Between the Pages</h3> <p>The library is empty. Dawn light through the tall windows. The painted constellations on the ceiling turn slowly in the silence. Dust motes drift.</p> <p>Haeth is at his desk. He's not cataloguing. He's sitting with his hands folded, spectacles on the desk beside him, watching the door. He was waiting for me.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"Your Highness."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Haeth."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"I assumed you might come. People often return to libraries before significant events. The instinct to seek knowledge persists even when knowledge can no longer change the outcome."</div> <p>He stands — slowly, joints protesting. He walks to the restricted case. Opens it with his own key. Removes the blue-leather diary.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"I told you there was a letter between pages forty-three and forty-four."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"You did."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"I didn't tell you there was a second item. Between pages sixty-one and sixty-two."</div> <p>He opens the diary. Between the pages — pressed flat, preserved by the dry library air — is a flower. Small, white, star-shaped. Dried but intact.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"Moonflower," he says. "The primary ingredient in the transformation potion. Someone — the anonymous author of this diary, presumably — pressed it here after the Rite. A memento. A marker. The flower that changed them."</div> <p>He holds it out. The dried moonflower sits on his wrinkled palm, weightless and ancient and impossibly delicate.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"I've been keeping this for forty-three years, waiting for someone who needed it more than the book did."</div> <p>I take the flower. It's so light it barely registers in my hand. A flower from a ritual performed centuries ago, pressed between the pages of a diary by someone who underwent the same transformation I'm about to undergo, preserved by a librarian who understood that some things are more than historical artefacts.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"Keep it," Haeth says. "Through the Rite and after. A reminder that someone walked this path before you and left a flower behind for the next person."</div> <p>I close my hand gently around it. The petals are dry and papery and they don't crumble because Haeth has spent forty-three years ensuring this library's climate is perfect for the preservation of fragile things.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Thank you, Haeth."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"Thank the person who left it. I merely stored it."</div> <p>He returns to his desk. Sits. Puts on his spectacles. Resumes the posture of a man who has been in this library for forty-three years and intends to remain for forty-three more.</p> <<set $d0_npc_haeth to true>> <<set $statWIS += 1>> <<set $statRES += 2>> <<set $stress -= 5>> <<set $hasMoonflower to true>> <<addItem "pressed_moonflower" "Pressed Moonflower" "A centuries-old dried moonflower, kept by Haeth for forty-three years, waiting for someone who needed it.">> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day0_library]] </div><h3>The Gossiping Maids — Different Pair</h3> <p>Two different handmaidens this time — older, more senior. They're not whispering. They're standing at the junction near the east wing, arms full of linens, speaking in low tones that aren't quite whispers but aren't normal volume either. The tone of people who know something significant is happening and are trying to process it through the lens of clean sheets.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MAID</span>"—Mistress Alva ordered the ritual chamber linens. The silver ones. Last used for the King's funeral preparation—"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MAID</span>"They're not for a funeral. They're for the Moonspire. I saw them being carried across the bridge this morning."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MAID</span>"The Moonspire? But those linens are for—"</div> <p>They see me. The silence is immediate but different from three days ago — not guilty, not startled. Sympathetic. These women know. Not the specifics, perhaps, but the shape of it. The palace has had three days to sense that something is coming, and the senior staff — the ones who've been here long enough to read the signs — have pieced it together.</p> <p>The older of the two curtsies. Deep. Formal. The kind of curtsy you give a prince, yes, but also the kind you give someone you might not see again in the same form.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MAID</span>"Your Highness. Safe travels."</div> <p><em>Safe travels.</em> Not <em>good morning.</em> Not <em>how are you.</em> Safe travels. As if I'm going somewhere far away. Which I am — farther than any ship could carry me.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Thank you."</div> <p>I walk on. Their silence follows me like a veil.</p> <<set $d0_npc_maids2 to true>> <<set $stress += 3>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day0_corridors]] </div><<npcPortrait "marta" "Marta">> <h3>Marta — The Last Pastry</h3> <p>She's been baking since midnight. The evidence is everywhere — every surface covered, every rack loaded, the output of a woman who processes anxiety through butter and flour. The kitchen staff move around her the way water moves around a boulder — with respect and without questioning the boulder's right to be there.</p> <p>She sees me in the doorway and stops. Sets down the rolling pin. Wipes her hands on her apron. She doesn't speak for a moment.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"Sit," she says. Her voice is different. Not softer — Marta doesn't do soft. But the usual declarative force is tempered by something. She points to the stool. My stool. The permanent one.</div> <p>I sit. She puts a plate in front of me. One pastry. Not cheese — apple, this time. Cinnamon and sugar and thin-sliced fruit in a latticed crust. She hasn't made apple pastries since I was twelve.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"I made your favourite," she says. "The one you used to beg for when you were little. Before you got too princely to beg."</div> <p>I look at the pastry. I look at Marta. Her eyes are red. She's been crying. Marta — who I have never, in twenty years, seen show anything other than volcanic confidence and wooden-spoon authority — has been crying in her kitchen at midnight while baking pastries from my childhood.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Marta—"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"Eat it. Don't talk. Just eat it."</div> <p>I eat it. The flavour is a time machine — twelve years old, sitting on this stool (it was taller then, or I was shorter), legs swinging, watching Marta roll pastry and telling her about my day in the breathless, overlapping sentences of a child who hasn't yet learned that adults don't always listen. She always listened. She listened the way she cooked — with full attention, with care, with the understanding that the thing being made deserved respect.</p> <p>The pastry is perfect. The cinnamon is warm. The apple is sharp. The sugar is sweet.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"Whatever happens today," Marta says, her back to me, stirring the pot that doesn't need stirring, "whatever changes — you come to my kitchen. You hear me? You come and sit on that stool and I will feed you. I don't care what you look like. I don't care what name you carry. You sit on that stool and you are my boy. Always."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I might not be a boy anymore, Marta."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"Then you'll be my girl. Same stool. Same pastries. Same Marta."</div> <p>I stand. I walk around the prep table. I hug her. She's solid — barrel-built, flour-dusted, smelling of butter and yeast and the particular warmth of a woman who has fed a palace for thirty years. She hugs me back. Hard. The wooden spoon presses against my shoulder blade. She's still holding it. Of course she is.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"Go," she says, releasing me, turning away so I can't see her face. "Go do what you need to do. And come back hungry."</div> <<set $d0_npc_marta3 to true>> <<set $energy += 10>> <<set $stress -= 10>> <<set $repStaff += 2>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day0_kitchen]] </div><<npcPortrait "nara" "Nara">> <h3>Apprentice Nara — Preparing the Chamber</h3> <p>She's on the stairs. Carrying candles — an armful of white wax pillars that she's struggling to balance. Her robe keeps catching under her feet. The enchanted music box is clipped to her belt, playing three notes on repeat — a fragment of the sympathetic resonance experiment, still not working right.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">NARA</span>"Your — oh! — Your Highness!" She wobbles. A candle slides. She catches it with her chin, which is both impressive and alarming. "I'm setting up the chamber. Ilara wants four hundred and twelve candles. Four hundred and twelve. Not four hundred, not four hundred and twenty — four hundred and TWELVE. Because apparently the magic cares about prime factors."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Four hundred and twelve isn't prime."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">NARA</span>"I KNOW! I told her that! She said it factors into sacred geometries that I'll understand in my sixth year. I'm in my third year. I have three more years of not understanding sacred geometries."</div> <p>She sets the candles down on a step. Catches her breath. Looks at me.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">NARA</span>"You're going through with it." Not a question. She's been in this tower long enough to read the signs.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I am."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">NARA</span>"Can I tell you something? Something I probably shouldn't?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Go ahead."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">NARA</span>"I was born with my left hand fused — the fingers webbed together. Couldn't grip, couldn't hold. The Silverveil fixed it when I was three. Transformation magic. Not the Rite — a smaller working, just the hand. But the principle is the same."</div> <p>She holds up her left hand. Five fingers, separate, functional. A faint silvery line runs between the ring and middle fingers — a scar, or a memory of one.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">NARA</span>"I don't remember having the webbed hand. I was too young. But my mother says I screamed for an hour after the working, and then I stopped, and I looked at my new hand, and I opened and closed my fingers for the rest of the day because I couldn't believe they moved separately. She says the first thing I gripped was a wooden spoon. Which is probably why I ended up in a tower full of tools and instruments."</div> <p>She picks up the candles again. Balances them against her chest.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">NARA</span>"It's going to hurt. I won't pretend it won't. But on the other side of the hurt, there are fingers that move. There's a hand that grips. There's a you that works in ways you can't imagine yet."</div> <p>She starts up the stairs. Pauses. Turns back.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">NARA</span>"Four hundred and eleven candles are set. You're my last trip. When I place this batch, the chamber is ready. For you."</div> <p>She climbs. The music box plays its three notes. The candles glow faintly in her arms, anticipating the fire.</p> <<set $d0_npc_nara2 to true>> <<set $stress -= 5>> <<set $silverveilFamiliarity += 2>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day0_moonspire_lower]] </div><h3>The Sword on the Wall</h3> <p>The training sword. Mounted above the desk on two iron pegs. Blade dull — it was never meant to be sharp. The grip worn to a polish by years of evening drills, the leather wrapping smoothed by palm sweat and repetition until it's as soft as skin.</p> <p>I take it down. Hold it. The weight is familiar — not heavy, not light, exactly what a practice sword should weigh. The balance point is six inches above the guard, where my index finger naturally rests when I grip for a thrust.</p> <p>I assume first position. Feet apart, sword extended, left hand behind my back. The stance is muscle memory — I don't think about it. My body simply knows where every part of itself should be in relation to the blade.</p> <p>I hold it for a long moment. Then I lower the sword. Set it on the desk.</p> <p>This body knows how to fight. The new body won't — not immediately. The muscle memory will be scrambled, the leverage different, the reach shorter by five inches. I'll have to relearn everything. Aldric will have to reteach me from the beginning, adjusting for a body that is lighter, shorter, with a different centre of gravity and narrower shoulders and—</p> <p>Breasts. I'll have breasts. How do you hold a sword with breasts? Is there a stance adjustment? Do the Silverveil teach that?</p> <p>The absurdity of this thought — standing in my chambers at dawn on the morning I'm going to have my entire body rewritten, worrying about sword grip with breasts — is so profound that I laugh. Once. A single, sharp, unhinged sound that echoes off the stone walls and comes back to me sounding exactly like a man losing his mind.</p> <p>I put the sword back. It can stay here. A relic. A reminder of the man who held it.</p> <<set $d0_npc_sword to true>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day0_chambers]] </div><<npcPortrait "vael" "Mistress Vael">> <h3>Mistress Vael — The Potion Is Ready</h3> <p>The Apothecary smells different today. The usual competing scents have been replaced by a single dominant aroma — silver and cold and floral and something underneath that smells like blood but isn't, quite. The moonflower essence.</p> <p>Vael is standing at her bench. Before her, a silver goblet. Ancient, plain, undecorated. Inside, the potion shifts between colours — silver, deep violet, near-black blue. It catches the light from the single window and refracts it into tiny rainbows on the stone walls.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">VAEL</span>"It's ready," she says. She doesn't turn around. "Brewed it overnight. Your blood was the last component — Ilara drew it while you were unconscious during your first visit." She pauses. "That sounds alarming. It was a small amount. Standard procedure. The magic needs to know who it's rewriting."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"You could have mentioned the blood-drawing."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">VAEL</span>"You had enough to worry about. A missing tablespoon of blood was not going to improve your day."</div> <p>She picks up the goblet. Holds it to the light. The potion ripples — not from movement, but from the magic inside it, which is alive, or something close to alive, vibrating with contained potential.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">VAEL</span>"This is you," she says. "Your blood, your template, your body's latent potential, combined with moonflower and silverveil silk and three hundred years of accumulated magical knowledge. When you drink it, it won't feel like taking medicine. It'll feel like swallowing a decision."</div> <p>She sets the goblet back on the bench. Looks at me.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">VAEL</span>"I've brewed a lot of potions in twenty years. Healing draughts, sleeping tinctures, love philters — don't tell anyone about the love philters — fertility aids, contraceptives, hangover cures. This is the first one I've made that will change someone's entire life in a single swallow."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Does that scare you?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">VAEL</span>"Yes." The bluntness. The honesty. Vael's gift. "But I checked it seven times. The ratios are perfect. The moonflower is peak potency. The blood integration is clean. If this potion doesn't work, it'll be because the magic failed, not because the brewing did. And I trust the magic."</div> <p>She hands me a small cloth pouch.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">VAEL</span>"Ginger root. Chew it after you drink the potion. It won't reduce the pain, but it'll keep you from vomiting, and vomiting wastes the potion and we'd have to start the brewing over and none of us want that."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Thank you, Vael."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">VAEL</span>"Don't thank me. Thank the moonflowers. They died for this." A beat. "That's an alchemy joke. They don't actually die. They're cultivated. Go. You're making the potion nervous."</div> <<set $d0_npc_vael2 to true>> <<set $statWIS += 1>> <<set $stress += 3>> <<set $riteKnowledge += 2>> <<set $hasGingerRoot to true>> <<addItem "ginger_root" "Ginger Root" "A small pouch from Vael — chew it after the potion to keep from vomiting.">> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day0_moonspire_lower]] </div><<npcPortrait "wynn" "Old Wynn">> <h3>Old Wynn — The Jasmine Survived</h3> <p>The jasmine survived.</p> <p>Wynn has uncovered it — the burlap pulled back, the branches exposed to the morning air. Three branches dead from the frost, cut clean and sealed with wax, exactly as he described. But beneath the dead wood: green. New shoots pushing outward from the core, finding light, reaching for the sky in directions the old branches never went.</p> <p>Wynn is standing beside it, trowel in hand, looking at the new growth with the quiet satisfaction of a man who bet on life and won.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">WYNN</span>"Your Highness." He doesn't turn. "The jasmine survived."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"You said it would."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">WYNN</span>"I said it might. Nature doesn't make promises. It makes attempts." He touches a new shoot — green, tender, pushing outward from where the dead branch was removed. "Different shape now. New directions. But smell it."</div> <p>I lean close. The scent — jasmine, sweet, heavy, unmistakable. The same scent it's always had. The same scent that fills the garden on summer evenings and drifts through the palace windows.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">WYNN</span>"Same flower," Wynn says. "Same roots. Same scent. Just wearing a new shape."</div> <p>He straightens. Looks at me. The sharp old eyes are bright with morning light and something kinder than wisdom.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">WYNN</span>"The frost was hard. Harder than I expected. But the core held. That's what matters, Your Highness. The core holds. Everything else is just branches."</div> <p>He hands me a sprig of jasmine — a fresh cutting from the surviving plant, three small white flowers still opening. The scent is immediate and overwhelming, a wave of sweetness that cuts through the morning cold.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">WYNN</span>"For the tower," he says. "Something alive, to take with you."</div> <<set $d0_npc_wynn3 to true>> <<set $statRES += 3>> <<set $stress -= 8>> <<set $hasJasmine to true>> <<addItem "jasmine_sprig" "Jasmine Sprig" "A fresh cutting from Wynn's surviving jasmine — something alive to carry into the tower.">> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day0_gardens]] </div><h3>The Last Erection</h3> <p>I wake hard.</p> <p>The body doesn't know about the Rite. The body doesn't know that in six hours it will be on an altar in a tower and the cock currently pressing against the mattress will be unmade and remade into something else entirely. The body only knows it's morning, and testosterone peaks at dawn, and the blood goes where the blood goes, and what it does when it gets there is what it's been doing every morning since puberty: filling the erectile tissue, engorging the shaft, lifting the cock from soft to rigid with the mindless efficiency of a system that runs on autopilot.</p> <p>I'm hard. Fully. The erection presses into the mattress — the familiar morning pressure, the weight of blood-filled tissue against linen, the head pressing against the fabric. I can feel it pulse — each heartbeat a tiny swell, the cock thickening and relaxing in rhythm with the circulatory system, a metronome of blood.</p> <p>I lie there. On my stomach. Cock trapped between my body and the bed. The pressure is warm. Pleasurable. The body is offering its simplest gift: an erection, unearned, unsolicited, delivered free of charge by biology that doesn't read calendars.</p> <p><em>This is the last time.</em></p> <p>The thought crystallises in the pre-dawn dark. The last morning erection. The last time I'll wake with this specific weight, this specific heat, this specific insistent pressure of a cock demanding attention. Tomorrow morning — if the female path — there will be nothing here. No weight. No pressure. No hardness. Just a smooth mound and the faint, unfamiliar awareness of a vulva I don't know how to feel yet.</p> <p>Or — if I choose differently — the cock will still be here. Changed, maybe. Enhanced, maybe. But present. Morning wood in a body that also has morning wetness. Both demands at once. The thought is dizzying.</p> <p>I don't touch it. Not this time. I lie in the pre-dawn dark and feel the erection exist. Just exist. The way you feel a heartbeat — not engaging with it, not manipulating it, just acknowledging the living pulse of a body that is doing what bodies do.</p> <p>It subsides on its own. Five minutes, seven. The blood retreats. The shaft softens. The morning wood gives way to morning. The last erection passes like the last star of night — not dramatically, not with ceremony, just a gradual dimming, an easing, a return to rest.</p> <p>I get up. I dress. The cock is soft against my thigh. Present. Warm. Mine.</p> <p>For six more hours.</p> <<set $d0_npc_morningwood to true>> <<set $stress += 5>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day0_chambers]] </div><h3>The Queen's Gift</h3> <p>Two knocks. Soft. Deliberate. Not Brin's nervous tap. Not Rowan's coded three-and-two. He never really does.</p> [[Speak with him|day-1_npc_haeth]] </div> <</if>> <<if (not $d2_npc_vaelin or $d1_npc_vaelin2) and $d1_npc_haeth>> <p class="empty-note">The library holds its usual hush. The constellations turn slowly on the ceiling.</p> <</if>> <div class="nav-return"> [[← Return to Palace Hub|day-1_hub]] </div><div class="scene-image"><<locationImage "moonspire_tower" "Moonspire Tower">></div> <h2>Moonspire Tower Meeting Ilara</h2> <p>The covered bridge is thirty paces long and feels like three hundred.</p> <p>Below me, the river crashes through the chasm with a sound like the world clearing its throat. The wind funnels through the gap and hits me broadside cold, sharp, carrying spray that tastes of mineral and deep earth. I grip the stone railing. The stone is ancient, worn smooth by centuries of hands that have crossed this bridge for the same reason: because the tower holds answers that the palace cannot.</p> <p>The Moonspire Tower rises from the eastern cliff like a single pale bone pointing at the sky. It's white stone not painted, not plastered, but quarried from something that naturally holds light. Even now, in the grey midday overcast, the tower has a faint luminescence, as if moonlight has been trapped in its walls and leaks out slowly, perpetually, regardless of the hour. It shouldn't be beautiful. It is.</p> <p>The door is arched, carved with symbols I don't recognise spiralling forms that could be letters or could be the visual representation of magic itself, frozen in stone. It opens before I touch it. I choose not to find that alarming.</p> <p>Inside: cool air, a temperature drop that has nothing to do with season and everything to do with whatever enchantments keep this place. The smell is layered dried herbs, old parchment, beeswax candles, and beneath it all something electric, something that makes the hairs on my forearms stand up and the back of my teeth itch. Magic. I've been around it my whole life the Silverveil maintain the palace wards, heal the soldiers, advise the crown on matters of the arcane but I've never been inside their tower. I've never been this close to the source.</p> <p>Stairs spiral upward, hugging the inner wall. Tapestries hang between sconces scenes of transformation, not all of them human. A serpent becoming a river. A tree becoming a woman. A bird becoming a song. The images shift slightly when I'm not looking directly at them, as if they're being retold each time the viewer blinks.</p> <p>I climb. My boots echo on stone that seems to absorb the sound and release it back half a second later, a faint auditory shadow that makes every step feel doubled. One flight. Two. Three. The stairs open onto a landing, and she's there.</p> <p>Archsorceress Ilara.</p> <p><<npcPortrait "ilara" "Archsorceress Ilara">>She's standing in the doorway of what must be the Ritual Chamber I can see, beyond her, a round room with a domed ceiling painted in stars and a stone altar at the center, low and wide, draped in silvery cloth. She's framed by the doorway like a portrait, and the effect is clearly intentional. Everything about Ilara feels intentional.</p> <p>Thirty-eight, according to the palace records. She looks it and she doesn't her face is sharp-featured, high-cheekboned, the kind of face that will look essentially the same at sixty as it does now because the bones are doing all the work. Dark hair shot through with silver, pulled back from her face and falling to her shoulder blades. Her eyes are the colour of rain on slate grey with a coldness that isn't unfriendly, just precise. She's wearing the Silverveil robes deep purple, silver-edged, fitted close to a body that is lean and straight-backed and radiates the particular calm of someone who has seen things that would break most people and chose not to break.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"You're here to ask questions," she says. Her voice is low, measured, the voice of someone who chooses every word and wastes none. "Not to commit."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"How do you know?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"Because you're standing in the doorway. People who've decided walk in."</div> <p>I look down. I am, in fact, standing precisely on the threshold one foot on the landing, one foot on the chamber floor, my body caught between entry and retreat. I step inside. It feels like a concession.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"Sit." She gestures to a chair near a small table where a teapot steams. The tea is poured before I've settled herbal, faintly sweet, with an undertone of something I can't identify.</div> <p>My first sip and the vice-grip in my chest loosens by a fraction. I look at the cup suspiciously.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"It's lightly enchanted," she says, reading my expression. "Not to influence your decision. To lower your cortisol. You're vibrating like a bowstring and I'd like to have a conversation with a human being, not a panic response."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I'm not panicking."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"You're breathing twelve times a minute and your jaw is clenched so hard I can hear your teeth grinding. In my professional experience, that qualifies."</div> <p>I unclench my jaw. Deliberately. She notices, and something that might be amusement crosses her face not a smile, exactly, but the ghost of one. The shadow a smile casts before the smile itself arrives.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"Ask your questions."</div> <p>I ask. She answers. Clinically at first the mechanics of the Rite, the preparation, the procedure, the timeline.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"The ritual takes approximately six hours to perform. You'll drink a preparation a potion brewed from moonflower essence, silverveil silk, and your own blood. The blood component is what personalises the magic it reads your body's current template and writes the new one. You'll lie on the altar." She nods toward it. "I and four sister sorceresses will channel transformation magic through your body over those six hours."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"The pain." It's not a question.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"Is significant. Not unbearable we manage it with enchantments, dampening fields that reduce the sensation to approximately forty percent of its actual intensity. Without the dampening, it would be unsurvivable the nervous system would shut down in self-preservation. With the dampening, it's... intense. Lord Aldren described it as 'being reforged on an anvil by the gods.' Prince Castien said it was 'the worst night of his life, followed by the first morning of his real one.'"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"That second one sounds like propaganda."</div> <p>That ghost-smile again.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"Castien lived as Princess Casta for forty-seven years. She was beloved. She was powerful. She was, by all accounts, happy. You can decide for yourself whether that's propaganda or outcome data."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Tell me about the physical changes. Specifically."</div> <p>She sets down her tea. Her hands fold in her lap long fingers, silver rings on three of them, nails trimmed short and practical. She speaks the way a surgeon explains a procedure: without hesitation, without euphemism, without apology.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"Your height will decrease by approximately five to six inches. Your skeletal frame will narrow at the shoulders and widen at the pelvis. Your musculature will soften and redistribute less mass in the upper body, more in the hips and thighs. Your facial bone structure will shift: jawline softens, cheekbones lift, brow ridge smooths, lips become fuller. Your hair will grow both in length and in density. Your body hair will thin considerably; your facial hair will cease entirely.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"Your skin will change thinner, softer, with increased sensitivity. Your fat distribution will shift to the breasts, hips, buttocks, and thighs. Your voice will rise the larynx will reshape, the vocal cords will thin and tighten.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"Your reproductive organs will change completely."</div> <p>She pauses here not for effect, but to give me a moment. I don't take it. I stare at her and wait. She continues.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"Your testes will be absorbed by the body. Your penis will reconfigure into a clitoris and labia the tissue is homologous, so the magic works with existing structures rather than creating from nothing. A vaginal canal will form, along with a cervix, uterus, and ovaries. You will be capable of menstruation and pregnancy.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"Breast tissue will begin developing during the ritual and will continue growing naturally over the following weeks and months. You'll wake from the Rite at approximately a large A-cup. Growth from there follows a roughly natural timeline, accelerated somewhat by the residual magic."</div> <p>My tea is cold. I'm not sure when that happened. My hands are wrapped around the cup, gripping it the way you grip something to prove you're still in control of your fingers.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"The transformation is permanent," she says. "There is no reversal. The magic rewrites you at the level of blood and bone. Your chromosomes will change. You will be female not a man made to resemble a female, not an illusion, not a disguise. Female. Indistinguishable from any woman born as one."</div> <p>Silence. The candles in the chamber burn without flickering enchanted flames, steady, unbothered by the chaos in my chest.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"The previous subjects," I manage. "They survived."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"All three."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"And after. Were they... themselves? Still?"</div> <p>She looks at me. For the first time, something in her expression shifts the clinical precision softens, just slightly, and I see what might be compassion. Or might be the memory of something she's seen before in this room, in those eyes, in the face of someone sitting where I'm sitting and asking the question I'm asking.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"You will still be you. Your mind, your memories, your personality, your preferences, your humour, your stubbornness" yes, she says that deliberately "will remain unchanged. You will think the same thoughts. You will recognise yourself. The body will be different. The person wearing it will be the same."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"She chose it to escape," I say. "Casta. She didn't choose it to be happy."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"No. She chose it to survive. And then she lived. As we all do making something of what we didn't choose."</div> <p>I set the cup down. Stand. My legs hold me, which feels like more of an accomplishment than it should.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I haven't decided."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"The door is always open." She walks me to the landing. At the top of the stairs, she stops. "Until it isn't. The next lunar alignment is tomorrow night. After that, three months. By then "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"By then my mother is dead and Vareth is king."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ILARA</span>"Yes."</div> <p>I descend the stairs. The tapestries shift as I pass the serpent becoming the river, the tree becoming the woman, the bird becoming the song. The images feel less like illustrations and more like previews.</p> <p>The bridge is colder on the way back. The river below sounds louder. If you walk toward the tower, I'll walk with you."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"You don't have to "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ROWAN</span>"No. But I'm going to. Because that's what friends do they walk you to the places you're afraid to go, and they wait outside, and they're there when you come out the other side."</div> <p>The door closes. The room is quiet.</p> <!-- --- STAT CHANGES --- --> <<set $stress -= 20>> <<set $statRES += 2>> <<set $affRowan += 10>> <!-- --- ADVANCE TIME --- --> <<set $timeSlot to "NIGHT">> <!-- --- UPDATE OBJECTIVES --- --> <<set $d1_rowan to true>> <<completeObjective "chambers_rowan">> <<addObjective "mirror_last" "The mirror. One last time." "MAIN">> <<addObjective "perrin_night" "The corridor Perrin is at his post" "SIDE">> <<if not $d1_npc_rowan_desire>> <div class="interaction-card side"> <h4>🔥 Ask the Question</h4> <p>"Rowan. When I'm... different. When I have a woman's body. Will you still..." You can't finish. But they know what you're asking.</p> [[Ask → |day-1_scene_rowan_desire]] </div> <</if>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-1_hub]] </div><<locationImage "servant_quarters" "Servant Quarters">> <h2>🔑 Servant Quarters Below Stairs</h2> <p>Alva's intelligence network. The machinery runs. It sees everything.</p> <<completeObjective "servants_alva">> <<if $d2_npc_alva and not $d1_npc_alva2>> <div class="interaction-card side"> <<npcPortrait "alva" "Mistress Alva">> <h4>🗝 "I Have Three Items"</h4> <p>She's expecting you. She's always expecting you.</p> [[Speak with her|day-1_npc_alva2]] </div> <</if>> <<if not $d2_npc_alva or $d1_npc_alva2>> <p class="empty-note">The household runs quietly on, unseen and essential.</p> <</if>> <div class="nav-return"> [[← Return to Palace Hub|day-1_hub]] </div><<day0Init>> <<set $energy to 60>> <<set $stress += 10>> <div class="day-transition"> <h2>Night. The last night.</h2> <p>You dream of the tapestries in the Moonspire. The serpent becoming the river. The tree becoming the woman. The bird becoming the song.</p> <p>In the dream, the bird is you. And the song is beautiful. And you can't remember what wings felt like.</p> <hr> <p class="transition-morning">Dawn comes. The morning of Day Zero.</p> <p class="transition-morning"><em>Today you walk to the tower. Today the Rite begins.</em></p> [[Dawn → |day0_wake]] </div><div class="scene-image"><<locationImage "training_yard" "Training Yard">></div> <h2>Training Yard Rage Session</h2> <p>I don't go to the training yard to train. I go to the training yard to break things.</p> <p>The practice dummy stands where it always stands a post wrapped in leather and stuffed with straw, shaped vaguely like a torso, with arms that swing when struck. It's been replaced a hundred times. I've destroyed a handful myself, on bad days. Today is a bad day.</p> <p>I grab a practice sword from the rack. Not the light one I use for sparring the heavy one, the one weighted with lead in the pommel that Aldric uses for endurance drills. It's too heavy for finesse. It's perfect for what I need.</p> <p>The first strike cracks across the dummy's left arm with a sound like a branch snapping. Straw erupts from a split in the leather. Good.</p> <p>I hit it again. Backhand. The dummy's head whips sideways, wobbles, comes back. I hit it before it's settled. Forehand, overhand, a diagonal strike that catches the torso and gouges a furrow through the leather. Straw bleeds out like intestines from a wound.</p> <p>I'm not sparring. Sparring requires technique, discipline, the careful architecture of offence and defence that Aldric has spent six years drilling into my muscles. This is the opposite of that. This is demolition. Every swing is the argument I can't win. Every impact is a door closing. The adoption crack. The bastard claim crack. The legal reform crack. The military option CRACK. The crumpled list in my pocket with every item crossed off CRACK CRACK CRACK.</p> <p>The dummy's left arm hangs by a thread. I sever it completely. It falls to the flagstones with a soft thump and lies there, straw leaking, pathetic.</p> <p>I keep going. The practice sword is heavier with every swing but I don't stop because stopping means thinking and thinking means the Moonspire and Ilara's voice saying <em>your testes will be absorbed</em> and <em>your penis will reconfigure</em> and <em>permanent, no reversal, blood and bone</em> and I cannot think about that right now. I cannot hold those words in my head and remain upright. So I hit things.</p> <p>Two hours.</p> <p>I know it's been two hours because the light has changed the midday overcast has broken and afternoon sun slants across the yard, catching the dust and straw I've launched into the air. My arms burn. The muscles from shoulder to wrist are screaming, not the productive burn of good training but the ragged, tearing protest of tissue pushed past its limits. Blisters have formed on my palms, split open, wept, and crusted. My grip is bloody. The practice sword is bloody. The dummy is gutted a skeleton of post and nails, straw scattered across ten feet of flagstones like the aftermath of a small, pointless war.</p> <p>I drop the sword. It clangs on the stone and the sound is very loud in the sudden silence.</p> <p>I sit. Right there, in the dirt, among the straw and the wreckage. My back against the empty weapon rack. My legs stretched out in front of me. My hands in my lap, palms up raw, blistered, streaked with blood and straw dust. My breath comes in ragged pulls. My heart is hammering so hard I can feel it in my throat, my wrists, the hollows behind my ears.</p> <p>These hands. I stare at them. Broad palms. Long fingers. Sword calluses built over six years of daily practice. The scar on the left forearm from the hunting knife. The ridge of tendon that stands up when I flex my wrist. Strong hands. A man's hands.</p> <p>In forty-eight hours, they could be different hands.</p> <p><<npcPortrait "aldric" "Aldric">>I don't look up when Aldric approaches. I hear him his boots on the flagstones have a particular cadence, heavy and even, the walk of a man who has never been in a hurry because he's always already where he needs to be. He sits down next to me without being invited. The fact that he's sitting on the ground at all Aldric, who treats military protocol the way priests treat scripture tells me he knows this is bad.</p> <p>He doesn't say anything for a while. We sit in the wreckage together. The afternoon sun warms the stone. A pigeon investigates the scattered straw with the blind optimism of a bird that has never considered the possibility that the world might not provide.</p> <p>He hands me a waterskin. I drink. The water is tepid and tastes of leather and it's the best thing I've ever put in my mouth.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDRIC</span>"I don't know what's troubling you, Your Highness." His voice is careful. Aldric's version of careful which means direct but gentle, like a sword sheathed in soft leather. "But I've served your mother for twelve years, and I know that look. It's the look of someone being asked to carry something too heavy."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"What if the weight is... everything I am?"</div> <p>He considers this. Aldric considers things the way he fights thoroughly, without rushing, with the understanding that a wrong response is worse than a slow one.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDRIC</span>"Then you carry it until your legs learn it. That's all any of us do."</div> <p>Simple. Aldric is always simple not because he's stupid, but because he's stripped away everything that isn't essential. He sees the world as a series of duties, loyalties, and the spaces between them. He doesn't know what I'm considering. He doesn't need to. He sees a man in pain, and he sits beside him, and he offers water.</p> <p>It helps. Not enough. But it helps.</p> <p>He stands first. Offers his hand. I take it his grip is warm and calloused and strong and absolutely, utterly certain. He pulls me up.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDRIC</span>"I'll have someone replace the dummy," he says, looking at the wreckage with the expression of a man surveying a battlefield.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I think I owe the armoury an apology."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDRIC</span>"You owe the armoury three dummies. I'll add it to the requisition." The ghost of something warm in his voice. "Get some food. And wrap those hands the blisters will get infected if you leave them."</div> <p>He walks away. His back is straight, his stride is even, and watching him cross the training yard I think: <em>that man would follow me into fire. And I'm about to become something he may not recognise.</em></p> <!-- --- STAT CHANGES --- --> <<set $statPRO += 2>> <<set $stress -= 10>> <<set $affAldric += 3>> <!-- --- ADVANCE TIME --- --> <<set $timeSlot to "EVENING">> <!-- --- UPDATE OBJECTIVES --- --> <<set $d1_training to true>> <<completeObjective "training_rage">> <<addObjective "chambers_rowan" "Evening approaches return to your chambers" "MAIN">> <<addObjective "gardens_wynn" "The gardens Old Wynn is covering the roses" "SIDE">> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-1_training_hub]] </div><<locationImage "training_yard" "Training Yard">> <h2>⚔ Training Yard</h2> <p>Chalk and iron. The weapon rack. The training dummies stand like silent witnesses.</p> <<if not $d1_training>> <div class="interaction-card main"> <h4>🗡 The Heavy Practice Sword</h4> <p>The weighted one. Lead in the pommel. Too heavy for finesse. Perfect for what you need.</p> [[Take it|day-1_training]] </div> <</if>> <<if $d1_training>> <<if $d2_npc_tamsin and not $d1_npc_tamsin2>> <div class="interaction-card side"> <<npcPortrait "tamsin" "Tamsin">> <h4>🗡 Tamsin at the Dummies</h4> <p>She's back. Her form is better. The short backswing took root.</p> [[Watch|day-1_npc_tamsin2]] </div> <</if>> <<if not $d1_npc_voss>> <div class="interaction-card side"> <<npcPortrait "voss" "Sergeant Voss">> <h4>🛡 Sergeant Voss Drill Perimeter</h4> <p>A compact, broad woman watching junior guards with the stillness of a predator.</p> [[Approach|day-1_npc_voss]] </div> <</if>> <div class="interaction-card"> <h4>⚔ The Destroyed Dummy</h4> <p class="flavor-dim">A skeleton of post and nails. Straw scattered across ten feet of flagstones. One arm missing entirely. Your work.</p> </div> <<if not $d1_npc_fantasy and $timeSlot is "AFTERNOON">> <div class="interaction-card side"> <h4>💭 Intrusive Thoughts</h4> <p>Your body is wrung out. Your mind, unguarded, goes to places you don't want it to go.</p> [[Don't look away → |day-1_scene_fantasy]] </div> <</if>> <</if>> <div class="nav-return"> [[← Return to Palace Hub|day-1_hub]] </div><<npcPortrait "aldwyn" "Master Aldwyn">> <h3>The Royal Healer Master Aldwyn</h3> <p>I nearly collide with him at the junction where the east wing corridor meets the central staircase. Master Aldwyn the Royal Healer is moving fast for a man of sixty, his robes billowing behind him like he's being chased by his own urgency. He carries a leather satchel that clinks with glass vials, and his face has the particular expression of a physician who has bad news and is trying to outrun it.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDWYN</span>"Your Highness " He stops. Adjusts his grip on the satchel. The vials inside clink again, a small dissonant music. "I was coming to find you."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"The Queen?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDWYN</span>"Had a difficult night. The coughing episodes increased four between midnight and dawn. The third one..." He pauses. Aldwyn is a man who measures his words the way an apothecary measures doses precisely, with full awareness of their effect. "The third one was productive."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Productive." I hate medical euphemisms. They dress suffering in clean linen and call it clinical.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDWYN</span>"There was blood. More than I'd like. I've adjusted her tincture stronger anti-haemorrhagic, increased the pain management, added a sleeping draught for tonight." He looks at me. His eyes are tired. Physicians who care about their patients always have tired eyes, and Aldwyn has cared about my mother for fifteen years. "She's refusing to rest, of course. She's been writing correspondence since dawn."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Of course she has."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDWYN</span>"Your Highness... I know you're carrying a great deal. I won't pretend to know what she's asked of you I know only what falls within my remit, and my remit is her body, not her politics. But I need you to understand: the trajectory is not ambiguous. Four months was my generous estimate. I'm revising it. Three, perhaps. Perhaps less."</div> <p>Three months. The number drops into my chest like a stone into a well.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDWYN</span>"I'm not telling you this to pressure you," he continues, though we both know that's exactly what the information does. "I'm telling you because you have the right to know. Whatever decisions are before you they have less time than you think."</div> <p>He adjusts the satchel again. The vials clink. He bows perfunctory, the bow of a man who has too many patients and too few hours and continues down the corridor at his urgent clip.</p> <p>I stand at the junction. Three months. Maybe less. The corridor stretches in both directions toward the east wing and my mother, toward the central palace and the rest of my life, whatever shape that life takes.</p> <p>The junction feels metaphorical. I resent it for that.</p> <<set $d1_npc_aldwyn to true>> <<set $stress += 5>> <<set $statWIS += 1>> <<completeObjective "corridor_aldwyn">> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-1_corridors]] </div><<npcPortrait "alva" "Mistress Alva">> <h3>Mistress Alva Intelligence Update</h3> <p>Alva is reviewing shift schedules at her desk a plain oak table in a plain room that serves as the nerve center of palace household operations. She looks up when I enter with the expression of a woman who expected me and has already prepared.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALVA</span>"Your Highness. I have three items."</div> <p>She doesn't ask how I am. Alva doesn't trade in pleasantries. She trades in information, and she trades it efficiently.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALVA</span>"First: the Ashborne courier who visited the Elder Council yesterday also visited the palace solicitor's office. He delivered a document my staff couldn't determine the contents, but the solicitor's clerk mentioned the words 'succession challenge' and 'expedited hearing.' The formal challenge may come sooner than your mother expects."</div> <p>My jaw tightens.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALVA</span>"Second: Archsorceress Ilara requisitioned additional moonflower essence from the palace apothecary stores this morning. The quantity is consistent with ritual preparation. She also requested privacy enchantments for the Moonspire bridge sound-dampening wards, to be activated at her discretion."</div> <p>She knows. Alva knows, or has deduced enough to know. She doesn't say it. She doesn't need to.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALVA</span>"Third: the kitchen stores are at seventy-two percent capacity. Marta is baking at crisis tempo, which depletes flour and butter reserves faster than the normal supply rotation can replace them. I've ordered an emergency resupply from the market. I mention this because it's the only problem in this palace I can actually solve."</div> <p>The last sentence is as close to a joke as Alva gets. I almost miss it.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Thank you, Alva."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALVA</span>"Your Highness." She picks up her quill. Returns to the schedules. Then, without looking up: "The east wing linens are prepared. Whatever happens tomorrow the household is ready."</div> <p>The east wing linens. She's talking about the Moonspire. About the ritual chamber. About the bed where someone might wake up changed.</p> <p>She's prepared for it. The whole palace, whether they know the specifics or not, is preparing.</p> <<set $d1_npc_alva2 to true>> <<set $statAUT += 2>> <<set $stress += 5>> <<set $ashborneThreat += 1>> <<set $householdReady += 1>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-1_servants]] </div><<npcPortrait "haeth" "Haeth">> <h3>Librarian Haeth Quiet Wisdom</h3> <p>Haeth is at his desk. He's always at his desk. I'm beginning to suspect the desk is a part of him that if you removed Haeth from the Grand Library, the library would dim, the constellations on the ceiling would stop turning, and the books would close themselves in mourning.</p> <p>He doesn't look up as I approach, but he speaks.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"You read the restricted sources. Elise's key work."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"You know about that."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"I know everything that happens in my library. I know about the key. I know about the diary. I know that Brother Vaelin has been camping in section twelve for thirty-six hours and eating crumbs on my floor, which I find personally offensive." He turns a page of whatever he's cataloguing. "I also know why you were reading what you were reading."</div> <p>He looks up. Those sharp old eyes bright as a bird's, missing nothing, forgiving everything.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"I've been librarian here for forty-three years, Your Highness. I was here when your grandmother was queen. I catalogued the Silverveil Compendium myself I was the one who placed it in the eastern alcove, because the light there is best for reading difficult material and anyone consulting that particular volume would need all the help they could get."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"You placed it there deliberately."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"I place everything deliberately. A librarian's job is not to store books. It's to ensure the right book reaches the right person at the right time. You needed that book. It was where you could find it."</div> <p>He returns to his cataloguing. Then, without looking up:</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"The anonymous diary in the blue leather. The second subject of the Rite. You noticed it was anonymous."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Yes."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"I've spent thirty years trying to determine the author. I failed. But I found something else a letter, tucked between the diary's pages when I first acquired the volume, written in a different hand. It was addressed to no one. It said: 'I was afraid of becoming someone else. I became someone I was always meant to be. The fear was real. The becoming was realer.'"</div> <p>He closes his catalogue. Looks at me over his spectacles.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"That letter is still in the diary, Your Highness. Between pages forty-three and forty-four. If you need it."</div> <p>I don't go back to the diary. Not today. But I know it's there. Between pages forty-three and forty-four. A letter from someone who walked this road and left a torch burning behind them.</p> <<set $d1_npc_haeth to true>> <<set $statRES += 2>> <<set $statWIS += 1>> <<set $stress -= 5>> <<set $libraryLore to true>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-1_library_hub]] </div><<npcPortrait "marta" "Marta">> <h3>Marta's Worry Kitchen Redux</h3> <p>The kitchen is running at what Marta calls "crisis tempo" the particular accelerated rhythm that occurs when the Head Cook senses institutional distress and responds by cooking more aggressively. The output is staggering: bread in three varieties, two soups, a roast being turned on the spit by a sweating pot-boy, pastries cooling on wire racks, and what appears to be the beginning of a multi-layered cake of the kind usually reserved for state occasions.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"You're baking a siege supply," I say from the doorway.</div> <p>Marta wheels around, wooden spoon raised like a mace. She lowers it when she sees me not entirely.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"I'm baking because this palace is going to need fed, and I've never once seen a problem made worse by pastry." She points the spoon at the stool. It's the same stool from yesterday. I suspect it has been designated My Stool by permanent decree. "Sit. You didn't eat breakfast."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"How do you "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"Your tray came back untouched. The bread, the cheese, the meat all still there. Even Brin noticed, and Brin notices very little that isn't directly in front of his face."</div> <p>I sit. She puts food in front of me bread torn from a warm loaf, a bowl of thick soup that smells of onion and thyme and the kind of slow-cooked patience that can't be rushed. I eat because refusing Marta's food would require more energy than I have.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"The Queen's quarters went through four changes of linen last night," she says, not looking at me, stirring a pot that doesn't need stirring her thinking gesture, unchanged since yesterday. "Aldwyn ordered fortified broth at midnight. The extra guards on the east wing are rotating on four-hour shifts instead of eight."</div> <p>She's telling me what the numbers look like. The human cost, measured in laundry and soup and guard schedules. Marta doesn't deal in politics. She deals in the logistics of feeding and maintaining a palace, and the logistics tell a story that's harder to argue with than any legal brief.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"Whatever you're deciding, Your Highness," she says, finally turning to face me, her flour-dusted face set in an expression that's half maternal fury and half something gentler that she'd never admit to, "decide soon. The palace can feel it. When the crown is uncertain, the whole building holds its breath. And I can't cook on held breath."</div> <p>The soup is excellent. The bread is warm. The world is ending and Marta is baking a fortress of carbohydrates against the dark, and somehow this is the most rational response anyone has had to the crisis.</p> <<set $d1_npc_marta2 to true>> <<set $energy += 15>> <<set $stress -= 5>> <<set $repStaff += 1>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-1_kitchen]] </div><h3>Messenger from Lord Veltham</h3> <p>A palace runner intercepts me near the stairwell a lean boy of sixteen whose entire purpose is to carry messages at speed through the palace's labyrinthine corridors. He's breathing hard. He's also terrified, because delivering messages to the prince apparently ranks somewhere between "thrilling" and "potentially fatal" in the servant hierarchy.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">RUNNER</span>"Your Highness a letter. From Lord Veltham. Delivered to the palace gate this morning, marked urgent."</div> <p>He holds out a sealed parchment. The seal is green wax Veltham's sigil, a pair of crossed keys over a wheat sheaf. Lord Veltham is a minor lord from the agricultural provinces. Wealthy enough to matter. Not powerful enough to threaten. A reliable ally of the crown for two generations.</p> <p>I break the seal. The letter is written in Veltham's hand careful, formal, slightly trembling at the edges in a way that suggests he wrote it quickly and under stress.</p> <p><em>Your Royal Highness,</em></p> <p><em>I write with urgency and in confidence. Lord Ashborne has dispatched envoys to the northern provinces with proposals of alliance. Three houses have received formal visits this week Thornecrest, Wyld-Marsh, and my own. The proposals are framed as trade agreements, but the substance is political: support for Ashborne's succession claim in exchange for tax concessions, trade privileges, and territorial adjustments.</em></p> <p><em>I refused. Thornecrest refused. Wyld-Marsh is considering.</em></p> <p><em>I do not know the extent of Ashborne's diplomatic campaign, but the pace suggests urgency. He is moving quickly, as if on a timetable. Whatever your mother's advisors are telling you it may be more pressing than they know.</em></p> <p><em>Your servant in loyalty,<br>Lord Edric Veltham</em></p> <p>I fold the letter. My hands are steady. My stomach is not.</p> <p>Ashborne isn't just waiting for the Elder Council to rule. He's actively building his coalition. He's preparing for the transition as if it's already decided as if my mother's death is a scheduling matter and the aftermath is a business opportunity.</p> <p>Three houses visited in one week. How many more that Veltham doesn't know about?</p> <p>I need to show this to Mother. Or to her advisors. Or to </p> <p>I put the letter in my pocket. Next to the crumpled list with every item crossed off. Two pieces of parchment that together describe the exact shape of the trap I'm standing in.</p> <p>The runner is still hovering.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">RUNNER</span>"Reply, Your Highness?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Tell Lord Veltham: received, with gratitude. His loyalty is noted and will be remembered."</div> <p>The runner nods, bows, and sprints off. I watch him go and think about urgency, about timetables, about a kingdom being divided like property before the owner is even dead.</p> <<set $d1_npc_messenger to true>> <<set $statAUT += 2>> <<set $stress += 5>> <<set $ashborneThreat += 1>> <<set $hasVelthamLetter to true>> <<addItem "veltham_letter" "Lord Veltham's Letter" "A warning: Ashborne is building alliances ahead of the succession ruling.">> <<completeObjective "corridor_messenger">> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-1_corridors]] </div><<npcPortrait "nara" "Nara">> <h3>Silverveil Apprentice Nara</h3> <p>The tower's lower levels are where the apprentices live and study. I discover this by taking a wrong turn on the spiral staircase down instead of up, toward the bridge and ending up in a corridor lined with doors, each painted a different colour, each radiating a faint warmth that suggests personal enchantment.</p> <p>One door is open. Inside, a young woman sits cross-legged on the floor surrounded by books, crystals, and what appears to be a partially disassembled music box that is playing itself despite having no visible mechanism. She's nineteen, maybe twenty dark-skinned, close-cropped hair, wide brown eyes that go even wider when she sees me in her doorway.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">NARA</span>"Oh. Oh no. You're the you're him. The prince. Prince Edrin." She scrambles to her feet. A book falls. A crystal rolls. The music box hiccups and plays three notes backward. "I'm Nara. Apprentice. Third year. I please don't tell Ilara I was sitting on the floor, she says it's 'energetically irresponsible' but I can't think in chairs "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I won't tell Ilara."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">NARA</span>"Oh thank the Mother." She exhales. Then catches herself. "I mean welcome to the Moonspire. Are you do you need something? I can get Ilara, or "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I'm leaving, actually. I just took the stairs in the wrong direction."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">NARA</span>"Oh! Right. Yes. Up for the bridge, down for us. Common mistake. Well not common, because almost nobody comes here. You're the first visitor in... months? Ilara doesn't encourage socialising. She says it dilutes the magical focus. I think she just doesn't like people."</div> <p>I almost smile. The girl's nervousness is genuine and completely without agenda she's not performing, not calculating, not angling for favour. She's a student who's been caught sitting on the floor with a broken music box, and her primary concern is not getting in trouble.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"What are you working on?"</div> <p>Her face transforms. The nervousness doesn't disappear, but it's instantly subordinated to excitement the particular incandescent enthusiasm of someone asked about the thing they love.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">NARA</span>"Sympathetic resonance enchantment! The idea is that you enchant two objects so they vibrate in harmony what happens to one happens to the other. The music box is the test case. Soldiers even new ones understand that some things are worked out with a blade and not with words.</p> <<set $d1_npc_tamsin2 to true>> <<set $statPRO += 1>> <<set $stress -= 3>> <<set $repMilitary += 1>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-1_training_hub]] </div><<npcPortrait "vael" "Mistress Vael">> <h3>The Apothecary Mistress Vael</h3> <p>The Apothecary occupies a room on the tower's third level a circular chamber with walls lined floor to ceiling with shelves of glass bottles, ceramic jars, dried plant bundles, mineral samples, and things I cannot identify and am not certain I want to.
