Marta's domain.</p> <<if not $d2_npc_marta>> <span class="badge side">🗡 The Head Cook</span> <</if>> <<if $d2_npc_marta and not $d2_npc_joss>> <span class="badge side">🗡 The scullion has gossip</span> <</if>> [[Enter → |day-2_kitchen]] </div> <</if>> <!-- ========== GRAND LIBRARY ========== --> <<if $d2_queen>> <div class="loc-card<<if $d2_library>> visited<</if>>"> <<locationImage "grand_library" "Grand Library">> <h3>📚 Grand Library</h3> <p class="loc-flavor">Three stories of knowledge. Painted constellations on the ceiling. Answers, maybe.</p> <<if not $d2_library>> <span class="badge main">⚔ Research the Rite of Becoming</span> <</if>> <<if $d2_library and not $d2_npc_elise>> <span class="badge side">🗡 A librarian in the stacks</span> <</if>> <<if $d2_library and not $d2_npc_vaelin>> <span class="badge side">🗡 A scholar on the floor</span> <</if>> [[Enter → |day-2_library_hub]] </div> <</if>> <!-- ========== ROYAL BATHS ========== --> <<if $d2_queen and $timeSlot is "AFTERNOON" and not $d2_npc_bath>> <div class="loc-card"> <<locationImage "royal_baths" "Royal Baths">> <h3>🛁 The Royal Baths</h3> <p class="loc-flavor">Hot water. Steam. You need to wash the day off.</p> <span class="badge side">🗡 Lissara is on duty</span> [[Bathe → |day-2_scene_bath]] </div> <</if>> <!-- ========== SERVANT QUARTERS ========== --> <<if $d2_queen>> <div class="loc-card"> <<locationImage "servant_quarters" "Servant Quarters">> <h3>🔑 Servant Quarters Below Stairs</h3> <p class="loc-flavor">The machinery of royal life. Clean corridors, honest work.</p> <<if not $d2_npc_alva>> <span class="badge side">🗡 The Head Housekeeper</span> <</if>> [[Enter → |day-2_servants]] </div> <</if>> <!-- ========== ROYAL GARDENS ========== --> <<if $d2_library>> <div class="loc-card<<if $d2_gardens>> visited<</if>>"> <<locationImage "royal_gardens" "Royal Gardens">> <h3>🌿 Royal Gardens</h3> <p class="loc-flavor">Stone paths, night-blooming jasmine, a silver stag fountain. Someone is playing a lute.</p> <<if not $d2_gardens>> <span class="badge main">⚔ Follow the music</span> <</if>> <<if not $d2_npc_wynn>> <span class="badge side">🗡 The old gardener</span> <</if>> <<if not $d2_npc_harwick>> <span class="badge side">🗡 A perfumed ambush</span> <</if>> [[Enter → |day-2_gardens_hub]] </div> <</if>> </div><<locationImage "kitchens" "Palace Kitchens">> <h2>🍞 Palace Kitchens</h2> <p>Heat, steam, chaos. Three hearths blazing. The smell of fresh bread and rosemary.</p> <<completeObjective "visit_kitchen_am">> <<if not $d2_npc_marta>> <div class="interaction-card side"> <<npcPortrait "marta" "Marta">> <h4>👩‍🍳 Head Cook Marta</h4> <p>She spots you immediately. There's a stool, a plate, and a look that says sitting is mandatory.</p> [[Sit|day-2_npc_marta]] </div> <</if>> <<if $d2_npc_marta and not $d2_npc_joss>> <div class="interaction-card side"> <<npcPortrait "joss" "Joss">> <h4>🧹 The Scullion</h4> <p>A soot-covered boy appears at your elbow. He has news.</p> [[Listen|day-2_npc_joss]] </div> <</if>> <<if $d2_npc_marta and $d2_npc_joss>> <p class="empty-note">The kitchen hums on. Marta is back to commanding her domain. No one else needs your attention.</p> <</if>> <div class="nav-return"> [[← Return to Palace Hub|day-2_hub]] </div><div class="scene-image"><<locationImage "grand_library" "Grand Library">></div> <h2>Grand Library Research</h2> <p>The Grand Library of Crown's Rest is three stories of accumulated knowledge, stacked in shelves of dark wood that reach toward vaulted ceilings where painted constellations wheel across plaster skies. Dust motes drift in the slanted afternoon light like slow, aimless snow. The air smells of old paper, binding glue, leather, and the particular dry warmth of a room that has been closed for too long and opened too rarely.</p> <p>I come here more often than any prince should. That's according to Lord Merrick, the Master of Ceremonies, who believes a prince's time is better spent hunting, jousting, and "projecting vigour" whatever the hell that means. I come here because books don't bow, don't lie, and don't look at me like I'm a problem to be solved through strategic marriage.</p> <p><<npcPortrait "haeth" "Haeth">>The librarian, Haeth, watches me from his desk near the entrance. He's ancient seventy, maybe eighty, hunched like a question mark, with eyes sharp enough to read footnotes across the room. He doesn't speak unless spoken to, which makes him the best conversationalist in the palace.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Haeth. I need everything you have on the Rite of Becoming. The Silverveil's transformation ritual."</div> <p>One white eyebrow rises. It's the most expressive I've ever seen him.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"Section nine, eastern alcove, top shelf. Three sources the Chronicle of Fairsworn, the Silverveil Compendium, and an anonymous account bound in blue leather that I've never been able to properly attribute. The succession law codices are in section three if you need those as well."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I do."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"They haven't changed since the last time you looked. Neither has the Founding Charter."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I know."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HAETH</span>"Yet you're looking again."</div> <p>I don't answer. He nods, as if my silence told him something, and returns to cataloguing whatever obscure manuscript has claimed his attention today.</p> <p>I find the books. The eastern alcove is quiet tucked behind a pillar, lit by a single tall window that faces the inner courtyard. A reading desk, scarred by centuries of scholars' elbows, sits beneath it.</p> <p>I start with the Chronicle of Fairsworn.</p> <p>Lord Aldren Fairsworn. Two hundred and eighty years ago. A minor lord from the coastal provinces, last male of a matrilineal line. His mother was dying. His sisters had been killed in a plague. The house would fall without a female heir. Aldren went to the Silverveil. The Rite was performed over seven days. Complete biological transformation. Aldren became Aldra. She bore two daughters in the following decade. Ruled for forty years. Died at seventy-one. The chronicle describes her as "a woman of formidable will who wore her second nature as though it had always been her first."</p> <p>The language is clinical in the sections describing the transformation itself. <em>The subject's physical form was reshaped in accordance with the ancient patterns height diminished, musculature softened, skeletal structure adjusted, reproductive organs replaced in totality.</em> In totality. I read that phrase four times. Each time it means the same thing and each time I understand it less.</p> <p>The anonymous account in blue leather is stranger. Less clinical, more poetic isn't the word. Raw. Written by someone who either experienced the Rite or spoke directly to someone who did:</p> <p><em>On the third day, I woke and my hands were not my hands. Smaller. The knuckles less pronounced. I held them before my face and thought: whose are these? Then, mine. These are mine and the grief was not for what I had lost but for how quickly the new thing began to feel like it had always been there, as if my body was a house and someone had rearranged the furniture and I hated it and also could not deny that the room made more sense this way.</em></p> <p>I close the book. My hands are shaking. I open them on the desk my hands, my current hands, sword-calloused and large, knuckles scarred from a hundred small injuries in the training yard. I flex my fingers. They respond. They're mine.</p> <p>For now.</p> <p>The Silverveil Compendium is drier magical theory, ritual components, success conditions. The Rite requires the subject's genuine consent ("coercion invalidates the pattern and the magic will not hold"), a lunar alignment that occurs every three months (the next one is in two days not a coincidence, I realize; Mother planned this), and seven days of sustained ritual during which the subject must remain within the Moonspire Tower.</p> <p>The succession law codices tell me what I already know: there is no loophole. No precedent for exception. No clever legal argument waiting to be discovered. Seven queens tried. Seven failed. The Charter is absolute.</p> <p>I sit among the books for a long time. The light shifts afternoon moving toward evening, the shadows of the shelves lengthening across the floor like dark fingers. At some point a junior librarian comes by with a candle and sets it on the desk without speaking. I don't remember thanking her. I hope I did.</p> <p>The facts are these: my mother is dying. Without a female heir, the kingdom falls to a man who will strip it to the bone. Every alternative has been tried and has failed. There is one option remaining, and it involves surrendering the body I was born in for one I cannot imagine.</p> <p>I close the last book. I stack them neatly. Haeth will notice if I don't.</p> <p>The walk back through the library feels longer than the walk in. The painted constellations on the ceiling turn slowly in the candlelight an old enchantment, Haeth told me once, cast by a Silverveil sorceress two centuries ago because the Head Librarian at the time liked the idea of stars indoors.</p> <p>Stars indoors. Magic that rearranges the sky because someone thought it would be pleasant.</p> <p>Magic that rearranges a body because someone thinks it's necessary.</p> <p>I push through the library doors into the corridor. The evening air is cooler. Somewhere, someone is playing a lute.</p> <!-- --- STAT CHANGES --- --> <<set $statWIS += 2>> <<set $d2_library to true>> <!-- --- ADVANCE TIME --- --> <<set $timeSlot to "EVENING">> <!-- --- UPDATE OBJECTIVES --- --> <<completeObjective "research_library">> <<addObjective "follow_music" "The Royal Gardens someone is playing music" "MAIN">> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_hub]] </div><<locationImage "grand_library" "Grand Library">> <h2>📚 Grand Library</h2> <p>Three stories of books. Dust motes in slanted light. Haeth watches from his desk.</p> <<if not $d2_library>> <div class="interaction-card main"> <h4>📖 Eastern Alcove The Rite of Becoming</h4> <p>Haeth directed you here. Three sources on the top shelf.</p> [[Research|day-2_library]] </div> <</if>> <<if $d2_library>> <<if not $d2_npc_elise>> <div class="interaction-card side"> <<npcPortrait "elise_librarian" "Elise">> <h4>📜 A Voice Between the Shelves</h4> <p>Someone is sorting books nearby. Ink-stained fingers, sliding spectacles.</p> [[Investigate|day-2_npc_elise]] </div> <</if>> <<if not $d2_npc_vaelin>> <div class="interaction-card side"> <<npcPortrait "vaelin" "Brother Vaelin">> <h4>📿 Scholar on the Floor</h4> <p>A young man in temple robes, surrounded by a fortress of open books, muttering about divine mandate.</p> [[Approach|day-2_npc_vaelin]] </div> <</if>> <<if $d2_npc_elise and $d2_npc_vaelin>> <p class="empty-note">The library has settled back into its usual hush. Nothing else here needs you today.</p> <</if>> <</if>> <div class="nav-return"> [[← Return to Palace Hub|day-2_hub]] </div><div class="scene-image"><<locationImage "palace_chambers_night" "Edrin's Chambers, Night">></div> <h2>Edrin's Chambers Night</h2> <p>My chambers are dark when I return. The fire has been rebuilt someone came in while I was out, despite my standing orders. I should be annoyed. I'm not. The warmth is welcome.</p> <p>I undress mechanically. Jerkin on the chair. Shirt over the back. Boots beside the bed, left then right, the way I've done since I was old enough to dress myself. The routine is comforting in a way that feels pathetic like clinging to a ritual because the world outside the ritual has stopped making sense.</p> <p>I stand in front of the mirror in my smallclothes.</p> <p>I don't know why. I didn't plan to. But my hands are taking stock, running an inventory that feels suddenly urgent, as if I need to record what's here before it changes.</p> <p>My shoulders. Broad. The muscle dense from years of daily training not bulky, more like cables wound tight under the skin. I roll them back. They move the way they've always moved.</p> <p>My chest. Flat. Defined. I can see the ladder of my ribs when I breathe in deep, the valley of my sternum, the faint trail of dark hair that runs from navel to the waistband of my smallclothes.</p> <p>My arms. Long. Lean. A scar on the left forearm where a hunting knife slipped when I was sixteen. My hands I hold them up. Large palms, long fingers, calluses on the grip-line from thousands of hours with a sword. These hands have held blades, quills, reins. Have gripped Aldric's arm after a good bout. Have pressed flat against my mother's cheek when she cried and pretended she wasn't.</p> <p>My jaw. I touch it. Sharp angle. The scratch of stubble that wasn't there this morning. My throat Adam's apple, prominent, the thing that bobs when I swallow hard.</p> <p>Below. I'm aware of the weight of my cock, soft against my thigh. Unremarkable. Warm. Mine. I don't touch it not like that, not tonight. I just... acknowledge it. The way you acknowledge a room you've lived in your whole life when someone tells you you might be moving.</p> <p>This body has been mine for twenty years. It is the only home I have ever known. It is strong and imperfect and I have never thanked it for anything and I have never had to because it was always going to be here.</p> <p>Two days.</p> <p>I get into bed. The sheets are cold, then warm. The fire crackles. Outside, very faintly, I can hear Rowan playing they must be in the guest quarters overlooking the garden. Something without a melody, just chords, drifting.</p> <p>I think about my mother's eyes. The fire in them. The certainty. She's already decided. She decided before she called me. The two days aren't for her to make up her mind they're for me to arrive at the conclusion she's already reached.</p> <p>I think about Lord Vareth Ashborne. I've met him twice. A large man with a smile that doesn't reach his eyes and hands that grip too hard when he shakes yours. His plans for the kingdom are no secret taxes doubled, military expansion, the common people pressed into service or poverty. He'd be a king of wolves, and the sheep would bleed.</p> <p>I think about the anonymous account in blue leather. <em>Whose are these? then, mine.</em></p> <p>I think about Rowan's words. <em>Finding out which parts were real all along.</em></p> <p>I think about the water dream that woke me this morning the cold closing over my head, the half-second of not knowing whether I was sinking or rising. I didn't think about it again, all day. There wasn't room. Now it's the only thing in the room with me.</p> <p>I don't sleep until the hour before dawn and in that single hour, I dream of water again a deep, warm pool, and I'm sinking into it, and it's closing over my head, and I can't tell if I'm drowning or being born.</p> <!-- --- STATE CHANGES --- --> <<set $d2_night to true>> <<completeObjective "return_chambers">> <<addObjective "sleep_d2" "Sleep" "MAIN">> <div class="scene-end"> <<link "Sleep →" "day-2_sleep_transition">> <<completeObjective "sleep_d2">> <</link>> </div><div class="scene-image"><<locationImage "queen_chambers" "Queen's Chambers">></div> <h2>Queen's Chambers The Truth</h2> <p>The corridor to the east wing is long and gets longer every time I walk it. Portraits line the walls my grandmother in battle armour, her mother in a coronation gown, her mother's mother on horseback with a falcon on her wrist. Every painting is a woman. Every queen, an unbroken line stretching back six hundred years to the Founding.</p> <p>At the end of that line: me. A man. The crack in the chain.</p> <p>More guards than usual flank the oak door to Mother's chambers. They bow. I nod. One of them a young soldier I don't know, barely old enough to shave looks at me with something that might be pity. I hate it immediately.</p> <p>The door is heavy. Carved with the royal crest: a silver stag beneath a crescent moon. I push it open.</p> <p>Inside: dim. The curtains are drawn against the daylight, which means it's a bad day. Mother only blocks the sun when the light hurts her eyes, and the light only hurts her eyes when the illness is flaring and the healers have given her the strong tinctures that make her pupils wide and fragile.</p> <p>The smell hits me. Medicinal herbs rosemary, meadowsweet, something sharp and astringent I don't know the name of. Honey, because the healers mix it into everything to mask the taste of the bitter draughts and beneath all of it, quiet as a secret, the copper-sweet rot. The smell of her body consuming itself from the inside.</p> <p><<npcPortrait "seraphina" "Queen Seraphina">>She sits propped against a fortress of pillows, a writing desk balanced across her lap. Papers everywhere she's been working. Of course she has. Queen Seraphina does not lie in bed and wait to die. She lies in bed and governs, and woe to the minister who assumes her horizontal position indicates diminished authority.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"Close the door. Sit. Don't argue until I finish."</div> <p>Her voice. Even now, even thinned by illness and the draughts that make her tongue slow, her voice has the quality of a drawn bowstring controlled tension, the promise of release. I grew up obeying that voice. I sit.</p> <p>She studies me. Those eyes grey-blue, same as mine, the one thing the portraits all share across six centuries of queens. Hers are sunken now, ringed dark, but the fire in them could smelt iron.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"How much do you know about the succession law?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Maternal line. Eldest daughter inherits. Unbroken for "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"Six hundred and twelve years and do you know why the Elder Council has refused every attempt to alter it?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Tradition. Prophecy. Stubbornness."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"The Founding Charter was signed in dragon's blood, Edrin. Whether that's literal or metaphor, it doesn't matter the Elder Council treats it as divine law. Seven queens have tried to amend it. Seven failed. I was the eighth. I failed three years ago, before the illness, when I still had political capital to burn. The Council said no. They will always say no."</div> <p>She lifts a document from the desk. Official seal. I recognise the Ashborne crest before she speaks.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"Lord Vareth submitted a formal succession claim last month. I've been blocking the hearing. I can block it for two more days. After that, the Elder Council convenes and rules."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"They'll rule for Ashborne?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"They'll rule that without a female heir, the crown passes to the nearest eligible house. Which is Ashborne. Yes."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Then we fight. We rally the bannermen "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"Vareth has alliances with Tormark, Veldain, and the Free Cities of the Sarrow Coast. Combined forces: twelve thousand professional soldiers. We can field seven thousand, and two thousand of those are garrison troops who haven't fought since the border skirmish nine years ago. The military analysis is not ambiguous, Edrin. If we fight, we lose. Not might lose. Will lose. Within eight weeks."</div> <p>The room is very quiet. I can hear the candle flames guttering. I can hear my own heartbeat, stupidly loud.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"What about a political marriage? Adopt a girl from another house, marry her to "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"Non-blood heirs have no claim under the Charter. It was tried in the fourth century. The resulting civil war killed twenty thousand people."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Legitimise a cousin. Father's side "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"Your father was an only child from a minor house with no living relatives. I checked. Twice."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Change the Elder Council. Replace them with "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"Appointed for life by the previous Council. Self-perpetuating. I can't remove them without cause, and 'they disagree with me' isn't cause."</div> <p>Every door I open, she's already closed. Every escape route, already bricked shut. She's not presenting a problem she's presenting a verdict and she knows it. I can see it in the way she watches me: patient, certain, and underneath it all, devastated.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"There is one alternative."</div> <p>She tells me about the Rite of Becoming.</p> <p>The Silverveil. The Moonspire Tower. Archsorceress Ilara, who she's already spoken with. The Rite ancient, forbidden, performed three times in recorded history. Each time, the subject survived. Each time, the transformation was permanent. Complete. Total.</p> <p>She tells me what it means. What it would do to my body. What I would become.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"In every legal, biological, and magical sense you would be my daughter. The succession holds. The Ashbornes have no claim. The kingdom survives."</div> <p>I stare at her. The candles flicker. Somewhere in the palace, a clock chimes noon, and the sound seems to come from very far away, from a world where things make sense and mothers don't ask their sons to </p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"You're asking me to stop being your son."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"I'm asking you to save everything I've lived for. Everything your grandmother lived for. Everything your great-grandmother bled for on the battlefield at Thornridge."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"By becoming a <em>woman</em>?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"By becoming the heir this kingdom needs."</div> <p>The words hang in the air between us. They have weight I can feel them pressing on my chest, on my ribs, on the lungs that suddenly aren't working the way lungs should work. I'm not breathing. I am, but it doesn't feel like it.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I need to think."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"You have two days. Then Vareth files his formal challenge, and the Elder Council rules. After that, no Rite, no ritual, no magic in the world will matter. The law will have spoken."</div> <p>I stand. My legs work, which surprises me. I walk to the door. My hand finds the handle through some miracle of muscle memory because my vision has gone narrow and strange, like looking down a long corridor.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"Edrin."</div> <p>I stop. Don't turn.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERAPHINA</span>"I didn't do this to you. The world did this. I'm just the one who refuses to pretend it isn't happening."</div> <p>I leave. I don't slam the door. I want to. I want to put my fist through the ancient oak and feel my knuckles split and bleed because at least that would be a pain I chose, a pain that makes sense, a pain with a clear cause and a clear end.</p> <p>Instead I press my forehead against the cold stone of the corridor wall. I breathe. In, out. In, out. The stone smells like nothing. Like minerals and centuries and the accumulated indifference of rock that has stood here long before I was born and will stand long after I'm dust.</p> <p>Two days.</p> <p>Two days to decide whether I lose my body or my kingdom.</p> <!-- --- STAT CHANGES --- --> <<set $stress += 35>> <<set $affSeraphina += 3>> <<set $loreSuc += 1>> <<set $d2_queen to true>> <!-- --- ADVANCE TIME --- --> <<set $timeSlot to "AFTERNOON">> <!-- --- UPDATE OBJECTIVES --- --> <<completeObjective "queen_summons">> <<addObjective "research_library" "Seek answers the Grand Library holds records of the Rite" "MAIN">> <<addObjective "explore_servants" "Explore the servant quarters Below Stairs" "SIDE">> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_hub]] </div><<locationImage "servant_quarters" "Servant Quarters">> <h2>🔑 Servant Quarters Below Stairs</h2> <p>Clean corridors beneath the palace. The machinery of royal life.</p> <<completeObjective "explore_servants">> <<if not $d2_npc_alva>> <div class="interaction-card side"> <<npcPortrait "alva" "Mistress Alva">> <h4>🗝 Mistress Alva</h4> <p>The Head Housekeeper. Iron-grey hair, ramrod posture. She doesn't curtsy. She never curtsies.</p> [[Speak with her|day-2_npc_alva]] </div> <</if>> <<if $d2_npc_alva>> <p class="empty-note">The servants go about their work. You're not supposed to be here, and lingering would make them uncomfortable.</p> <</if>> <div class="nav-return"> [[← Return to Palace Hub|day-2_hub]] </div><<day1Init>> <<set $energy to 80>> <<set $stress += 5>> <div class="day-transition"> <h2>Night passes. You don't sleep until the hour before dawn.</h2> <p class="transition-morning">In that single hour, you dream of water a deep, warm pool, and you're sinking into it, and it's closing over your head, and you can't tell if you're drowning or being born.</p> [[Dawn breaks. → |day-1_hub]] </div><div class="scene-image"><<locationImage "training_yard" "Training Yard">></div> <h2>Training Yard Morning Drill</h2> <p>The training yard smells the way it always smells iron, leather, sweat, and the particular dusty chalk they spread on the flagstones to keep the footing honest. Morning light slants across the open square, catching the edge of practice blades lined up on the rack like surgical tools.</p> <p><<npcPortrait "aldric" "Aldric">>Aldric is already here. Of course he is. I'm convinced the man sleeps standing up in his armour somewhere in the barracks and simply opens his eyes when the sun touches the horizon. He's running a whetstone along his practice blade not because it needs sharpening, practice blades are intentionally dull, but because the motion calms him. I've watched him do it before every spar for six years.</p> <p>He's tall. Taller than me by two inches, which irritates me more than it should. Broad across the shoulders and chest, built like something designed for the specific purpose of breaking other things. A scar runs from his left temple to his jaw a bandit's knife, three years ago, when he threw himself between me and a blade during a hunting trip. I told him that was unnecessary. He told me it was literally his job. We didn't speak for two days because we were both right.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDRIC</span>"Your Highness." He sets down the whetstone. Stands. The motion is economical no wasted energy, no theatrical flourish. Aldric moves the way a sword cuts: direct.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Captain."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDRIC</span>"You look like hell."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Thank you, Aldric. Your gift for courtly flattery remains unmatched."</div> <p>The ghost of a smile. He hands me a practice blade weighted steel, edge rounded, heavy enough to simulate the real thing without removing limbs. I take it. The grip is familiar. My palm fits the leather wrapping the way a key fits a lock.</p> <p>We circle. The yard is empty this early just us and the pigeons on the battlement. The air is cool. My breath comes in thin clouds.</p> <p>Aldric moves first. A testing strike high, right side, the kind you can read from across a continent. I parry. Turn it. Riposte. He blocks without looking, which is the most insulting thing a swordsman can do to another swordsman, and steps inside my guard.</p> <p>My mind isn't in it. My mind is in my mother's chambers, in the copper-sweet smell of medicinal herbs that doesn't quite cover the other smell, the one the healers pretend doesn't exist. The smell of someone dying slowly.</p> <p>His blade touches my ribs. I didn't see the feint.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDRIC</span>"Dead," he says, stepping back.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Best of three."</div> <p>We reset. I'm faster this time anger is a decent substitute for focus, in short bursts. I catch his blade on the cross-guard, twist, drive forward. For half a second I see something in his eyes surprise, maybe approval. Then he drops his shoulder, pivots, and the flat of his practice sword cracks across my forearm hard enough to numb my fingers. My blade clatters to the flagstones.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDRIC</span>"Your mind isn't here, Your Highness."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"My mind is in my mother's lungs, where all the air seems to have gone."</div> <p>He doesn't say anything for a moment. Aldric isn't good with words he's good with silences, which is rarer and more useful. He picks up my blade. Hands it back, hilt-first.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDRIC</span>"She asked for you. This morning. The Royal Healer was summoned at dawn."</div> <p>So the servant wasn't exaggerating the urgency. Wonderful.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I know."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDRIC</span>"Go to her."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I was planning to."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALDRIC</span>"Go now. The swords will be here tomorrow."</div> <p>I sheathe the practice blade without cleaning it muscle memory, not disrespect, but I see Aldric's jaw tighten at the breach of discipline. Any other day he'd correct me. Today, he says nothing. He just watches me cross the yard toward the palace entrance, and when I glance back, he's standing exactly where I left him, hands clasped behind his back, face unreadable.</p> <p>The pigeons scatter as I pass. Somewhere in the kitchens, someone drops a pot. The morning goes on.</p> <!-- --- STAT CHANGES --- --> <<set $statPRO += 1>> <<set $stress += 5>> <<set $d2_sparred to true>> <<set $affAldric += 2>> <!-- --- ADVANCE TIME --- --> <<set $timeSlot to "MIDDAY">> <!-- --- UPDATE OBJECTIVES --- --> <<completeObjective "train_aldric">> <<addObjective "queen_summons" "Answer the Queen's summons Queen's Chambers, East Wing" "MAIN">> <<addObjective "explore_corridors" "Explore the corridors" "SIDE">> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_hub]] </div><<locationImage "training_yard" "Training Yard">> <h2>⚔ Training Yard</h2> <p>Chalk-dusted flagstones. Practice blades on the rack. Morning light.</p> <<if not $d2_sparred>> <div class="interaction-card main"> <<npcPortrait "aldric" "Aldric">> <h4>🗡 Captain Aldric Vane</h4> <p>He's running a whetstone along his practice blade. Waiting for you.</p> [[Spar with Aldric|day-2_training]] </div> <</if>> <<if $d2_sparred>> <<if not $d2_npc_keller>> <div class="interaction-card side"> <<npcPortrait "keller" "Guardsman Keller">> <h4>🛡 Guardsman at the Bench</h4> <p>A weathered soldier sharpening his sword. He looks like he wants to talk.</p> [[Approach|day-2_npc_keller]] </div> <</if>> <<if not $d2_npc_tamsin>> <div class="interaction-card side"> <<npcPortrait "tamsin" "Tamsin">> <h4>🗡 Recruit at the Training Dummies</h4> <p>A young woman beating a dummy with questionable technique but admirable fury.</p> [[Watch / Intervene|day-2_npc_tamsin]] </div> <</if>> <<if $d2_npc_keller and $d2_npc_tamsin>> <p class="empty-note">The yard is quiet now. Nothing else demands your attention here.</p> <</if>> <</if>> <div class="nav-return"> [[← Return to Palace Hub|day-2_hub]] </div><div class="scene-image"><<locationImage "palace_chambers" "Edrin's Chambers">></div> <h2>Edrin's Chambers Morning</h2> <p>I wake with water still in my lungs.</p> <p>Not real water I know that before I'm even fully awake, before my eyes have found the ceiling or my hands have found the edge of the blanket. But for one raw, disoriented second it's absolute: the pressure of it, the cold, the black closing over my head like a lid coming down. Then it's gone, and I'm just a man in a bed, heart going too hard for a dream I can't hold onto.</p> <p>I don't remember any of it. I never do. Just the water, and the specific, useless terror of not knowing whether I was sinking or rising.</p> <p>She's coughing now. Not that I can hear it from here. I just know. The way you know rain is coming when the air goes heavy and the birds stop singing.</p> <p>Grey light pushes through the arrow-slit windows. Dawn in Aethermere is never generous it doesn't flood in, doesn't announce itself with warmth. It seeps. A slow invasion of pale nothing that turns everything the colour of old iron.</p> <p>I swing my legs off the bed. Stone floor. Cold enough to make me hiss through my teeth. Someone let the fire die no, I told the servants not to tend it overnight. I don't like people in my rooms while I sleep. A prince's paranoia, Aldric calls it. A reasonable precaution, I call it. Not like anyone's tried to kill me. Yet.</p> <p>My chambers are... modest, for a prince. That's what the courtiers whisper, anyway, in that tone that makes "modest" sound like a disease. Bookshelves line two walls histories, treatises on statecraft, a worn collection of Thornridge campaign journals that belonged to my grandmother. A training sword hangs above the desk, blade dull but grip worn smooth from years of evening drills when the yard was occupied. Maps pinned to the wall the kingdom, the neighbouring territories, a crude sketch of the Ashborne lands I drew myself when I was seventeen and furious about something I can't remember now.</p> <p>The half-finished letter on the desk catches my eye. I started writing to Rowan three weeks ago. Got as far as <em>"The court is suffocating and I'm considering taking up goat herding as an alternative career"</em> before I lost the energy to be funny. The ink has dried in the nib.</p> <p>I dress. Linen shirt, leather jerkin the good one, with the reinforced shoulders, because I'm sparring this morning and last time I wore the thin one Aldric's practice blade left a bruise the shape of a crescent moon on my collarbone. Dark trousers. Boots. The boots are getting worn at the heels. I should have the cobbler replace them. I won't. I've broken them in perfectly and new boots are a betrayal of the feet.</p> <p>The mirror.</p> <p>I don't know why I stop in front of it today. I pass it every morning it's bolted to the wall beside the wardrobe, a sheet of polished silver in a dark wood frame. Most days I glance. Today I look.</p> <p>A lean man stares back. Dark hair falling over grey-blue eyes that my mother calls "storm-coloured," which is a kind way of saying they can't decide what they are. Sharp jaw, a little too sharp I haven't been eating enough, and it shows in the hollows beneath my cheekbones. Shadows under my eyes because I slept four hours, maybe five. Handsome, supposedly. Rosalind Thorne told me once I had "the face of a man who doesn't know he's beautiful, which is either charming or infuriating depending on my mood." I didn't know what to do with that then. Still don't.</p> <p>My shoulders are broad from six years of swordwork. Arms ropey rather than bulky I'm fast, not strong, and Aldric has trained me accordingly. I run my hand through my hair. It flops back immediately. I don't bother trying again.</p> <p>This is me. These bones and muscles and the rough scrape of stubble under my jaw that I should shave but won't because there's a petty satisfaction in looking slightly unkempt when the courtiers expect polish.</p> <p>I don't know why I catalogue it all this morning. Some instinct, maybe. The way you unconsciously memorize a room you're about to leave.</p> <p>A knock. The door opens a servant, young, nervous, carrying a tray. Bread, hard cheese, cold venison from last night's roast. A cup of something steaming that smells like it's trying to be tea and failing.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERVANT</span>"Your Highness. Breakfast."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"On the table."</div> <p>He sets it down. Lingers.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Something else?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">SERVANT</span>"The Queen's Healer was summoned at first light, Your Highness. Captain Vane asked me to tell you Her Majesty has requested your presence. At your convenience, he said, but..." He falters. "He said it the way he says things that aren't actually at your convenience."</div> <p>My stomach clenches. I nod. The servant leaves.</p> <p>I eat standing at the window. The bread is yesterday's slightly stale, the way I prefer it, because fresh bread is too soft and tears when you try to spread anything on it. Below, the courtyard is busy. Guards changing shift. Stable hands leading horses. A merchant's cart being inspected at the inner gate. Normal. Everything looks so bloody normal.</p> <p>The cheese tastes like nothing. I eat it anyway. Energy is energy.</p> <!-- --- STATE CHANGES --- --> <<set $d2_woke to true>> <<completeObjective "wake_up">> <<addObjective "train_aldric" "Report to the Training Yard morning sparring with Captain Vane" "MAIN">> <<addObjective "examine_chambers" "Examine your chambers" "SIDE">> <<addObjective "visit_kitchen_am" "Visit the Kitchens breakfast is better hot" "SIDE">> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_hub]] </div><<npcPortrait "alva" "Mistress Alva">> <h3>The Head Housekeeper Mistress Alva</h3> <p>The servant quarters sit below the palace's main level a network of clean, plain corridors where the machinery of royal life operates invisibly. Here is where the linen is pressed, the silver polished, the candles replaced, the fires laid. It's a world I'm not supposed to see and rarely do, which is exactly why I come here sometimes. It's honest work. No one is performing.</p> <p>Mistress Alva runs it all. She's fifty, severe, with iron-grey hair pinned under a white cap and a posture that suggests she was born standing at attention. She runs the household staff of eighty-seven people with the efficiency of a military commander and the warmth of a glacier. She terrifies everyone, including me, and she's been doing it since before I could walk.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALVA</span>"Your Highness." She doesn't curtsy she has never curtsied to anyone, as far as I know, on the grounds that bending wastes time. "This is an unusual visit."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I wanted to walk."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALVA</span>"You wanted to avoid the east wing corridor. The route through the servant quarters bypasses it entirely. I know. I designed the layout."</div> <p>She knows. Of course she knows. Alva knows the location of every person in this palace at any given moment. She's a human panopticon.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALVA</span>"Your breakfast was returned with the bread eaten and the cheese eaten and the meat eaten and the chair cold. You ate standing."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I did."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALVA</span>"Your mother ate lying down. She's been doing that more often. Her appetite is diminishing. The healers have shifted to fortified broths." Alva's voice is clinical. She reports facts the way a surgeon reports vital signs. "I've increased the laundry rotation for the east wing. The Queen's linens need changing more frequently now."</div> <p>I don't want to know this. I need to know this. These are the details that the ministers don't mention and the healers euphemise the physical reality of a dying woman's daily life, measured in linens and broths and the declining angle of a pillow stack.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Alva. Is there anything she needs?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALVA</span>"She needs a miracle or a successor. I can provide neither. I can provide clean sheets, hot broth, and a palace that runs smoothly enough that she can focus her remaining energy on governance rather than domestic logistics." A pause. "I can also provide information, should you require it."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Information?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALVA</span>"I oversee eighty-seven staff. They move through every room in this palace. They see things. Hear things. The east wing guards are on double rotation that I ordered, at the Queen's request. The Silverveil bridge was crossed by Archsorceress Ilara at dawn my staff reported it. Lord Ashborne's household sent a courier to the Elder Council this morning one of my laundresses is married to a Council clerk."</div> <p>She looks at me. There's no warmth in her eyes, but there's something else the fierce, unsentimental protectiveness of a woman who has served the crown for thirty years and considers its survival a personal responsibility.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALVA</span>"The household is loyal, Your Highness. Whatever comes."</div> <p>The same words Keller used. Different voice, same promise. The palace is circling its wagons, and they're doing it quietly, without being asked, because that's what loyalty looks like when it's real.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Thank you, Alva."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ALVA</span>"Don't thank me. Eat sitting down. You'll develop acid reflux."</div> <<set $d2_npc_alva to true>> <<set $statAUT += 1>> <<set $statRES += 1>> <<set $repStaff += 2>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_servants]] </div><<npcPortrait "brin" "Brin">> <h3>The Servant Brin</h3> <p>The servant lingers near the door after setting down the tray. He's young sixteen, maybe seventeen with sandy hair that sticks up on one side like he slept on it wrong and didn't have time to fix it. His livery is slightly too large. New hire. The palace takes them from common families as a form of patronage steady work, meals, a roof that doesn't leak.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">BRIN</span>"Is there anything else you need, Your Highness? More bread? I can get the fresh loaves from the kitchen Marta just pulled them, they're still steaming "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"The stale bread is fine."</div> <p>He blinks. Most princes, I imagine, do not prefer stale bread. I could explain the texture argument. I don't.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"You're new," I say instead, because his nervous hovering is going to outlast my patience.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">BRIN</span>"Third week, Your Highness. I'm Brin. Son of Tomlen the tanner. From the Lower Market district." He says it like he's reciting for an exam. "My mum said to be useful and not drop anything."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"How's that going?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">BRIN</span>"I dropped a soup tureen yesterday. In front of Lady Harwick. She made a noise like a horse being stepped on."</div> <p>I almost smile. Almost. "Lady Harwick makes that noise when her wine is the wrong temperature. Don't take it personally."</p> <p>He relaxes, marginally.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">BRIN</span>"The guards are saying... there's extra security on the east wing today. Is the Queen "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"The Queen is fine."</div> <p>The lie comes easily. Princes learn to lie before they learn to ride.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"She's meeting with advisors. Routine."</div> <p>He nods, wanting to believe it because the alternative is frightening. I know the feeling.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Brin."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">BRIN</span>"Your Highness?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"The fresh bread. Bring me a loaf for later and tell Marta I said her cheese pastries from last week were excellent."</div> <p>His face lights up. A small kindness it costs me nothing and gives him a story to tell in the servants' hall tonight. <em>The prince remembered the pastries. The prince knows my name.</em> These things matter to people who are rarely seen.</p> <p>He leaves with more confidence than he entered.</p> <<set $d2_npc_brin to true>> <<set $repStaff += 1>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_chambers_explore]] </div><<npcPortrait "caedric" "Ser Caedric">> <h3>Old Ser Caedric The Retired Knight</h3> <p>He's sitting in the alcove near the portrait gallery, where the old knights always sit a stone bench with a worn cushion that's been here since before I was born. Ser Caedric. Seventy-three. Retired from the Royal Guard twelve years ago when his knees gave out. He still wears his sword, though the palace wags say it's rusted into the scabbard.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"Prince Edrin." He doesn't stand. His knees won't allow it, and we stopped pretending years ago.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Ser Caedric."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"Sit with me a moment?"</div> <p>I shouldn't. I have places to be, things to dread, a future to collapse into. But Caedric served my grandmother. He carried me on his shoulders when I was three. He taught me to whittle, badly, and never once told me I was too old for it.</p> <p>I sit.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"You look like your mother. Same look she had the day your father died. Like the world has just told a terrible joke and you're still deciding whether to laugh."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I didn't know you knew my father well."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"I carried his coffin." Caedric's voice is matter-of-fact. Old soldiers talk about death the way bakers talk about flour a material they've worked with so long it's lost its mystery. "Good man. Quiet. Loved your mother more than anything, including himself, which is the only kind of love worth having."</div> <p>He adjusts his sword belt. The leather creaks.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"The palace is nervous today. Guards doubled on the east wing. Ilara sighted at the Moonspire. The kitchen staff are making comfort food always a sign of institutional anxiety. Marta makes cheese pastries when she's worried."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"You notice a lot for a man on a bench."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"I notice everything from this bench. It's the perfect surveillance position. Every corridor converges here. I've been monitoring palace morale from this spot since before you could walk." He gives me a look sharp, fond, knowing. "Whatever your mother told you today and she told you something, because you've gone grey around the eyes remember that the Thornridge queens survived worse. Your great-grandmother fought a war at nineteen with half an army and a broken sword. She won. Not because she was strong. Because she was stubborn."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Being stubborn and being strong aren't the same thing."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"They're not. But stubbornness is more reliable. Strength fails. Stubbornness just keeps showing up."</div> <p>He pats my knee with a gnarled hand.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"Go on. Do whatever it is you need to do. I'll be on this bench."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"You're always on this bench."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">CAEDRIC</span>"That's the stubbornness."</div> <<set $d2_npc_caedric to true>> <<set $statRES += 1>> <<set $stress -= 3>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_corridors]] </div><<npcPortrait "elise_librarian" "Elise">> <h3>Junior Librarian Elise</h3> <p>She finds me between the shelves. Or I find her hard to tell who was lost first. Elise is a junior librarian, one of Haeth's three apprentices, a nervous woman in her mid-twenties with ink-stained fingers and spectacles that keep sliding to the tip of her nose. She pushes them up approximately once every four seconds. I've counted.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ELISE</span>"Your Highness! I I didn't realise you were are you looking for something specific? I can "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I found what I needed, thank you."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ELISE</span>"Oh. Good. That's good." She pushes her spectacles up. Four seconds. "Only, I noticed you pulled the Silverveil Compendium, and I'm sorry, it's not my place, but there are two additional sources in the restricted section that Haeth might not have mentioned. A diary, attributed to the second subject of the Rite the unnamed commoner and a treatise by Archsorceress Vesper on the theoretical limits of transformation magic. Both are fragile and Haeth doesn't like people touching them, but you're well, you're the prince, so..."</div> <p>I stop. The diary of the second subject. The nameless commoner who disappeared from records.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Where?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ELISE</span>"Restricted case seven. The glass one near the spiral staircase. I can unlock it I have Haeth's secondary key." She flushes, as if admitting this is a confession. "He doesn't know I copied it. Please don't tell him."</div> <p>I almost smile.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Your secret is safe."</div> <p>She leads me to the restricted case. It's tall, iron-framed, glass-panelled. Inside, among other ancient documents, sit two items: a small leather-bound diary, cover cracked with age, and a thick manuscript bound in green cloth.</p> <p>Elise unlocks the case. Her hands are steady despite her nerves a librarian's hands, precise and careful.</p> <p>The diary is short. Most of it is water-damaged and illegible. But a few passages survive:</p> <p><em>I was nobody before and nobody after. That is the secret they do not tell you the Rite does not care who you are. It only cares what you are willing to become. I was willing. I am still deciding if that was courage or surrender.</em></p> <p><em>My body is a country I am still learning to navigate. There are borders I did not expect. Territories that surprise me. I map myself daily and the map is never finished.</em></p> <p>I close the diary. My hands are shaking again.</p> <p>Vesper's treatise is dense, theoretical, and largely incomprehensible without a Silverveil education. But one passage stands out:</p> <p><em>The Rite of Becoming does not create. It reveals. The body holds all possibilities; the Rite merely selects one and makes it dominant. This is why consent is required the subject must agree to become what they already, in some fundamental sense, are.</em></p> <p>I don't know what to do with that. I put both books back. Elise locks the case.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Thank you, Elise."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">ELISE</span>"Your Highness." She pushes her spectacles up. "If you need anything else anything at all I'm usually shelving in section twelve. The poetry section. Nobody goes there."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Noted."</div> <p>I leave her standing by the case, fingers on the iron frame, watching me go with an expression I can't read.</p> <<set $d2_npc_elise to true>> <<set $statWIS += 1>> <<set $stress += 5>> <<set $libraryLore to true>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_library_hub]] </div><<npcPortrait "harwick" "Lady Harwick">> <h3>Lady Harwick The Court Gossip</h3> <p>Lady Harwick materialises from behind a topiary like a well-dressed ambush. She's sixty, perfumed to the point of weaponisation, draped in enough jewelry to furnish a small treasury, and possessed of a smile that could mean anything from "delighted to see you" to "I'm going to destroy your reputation at dinner."</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HARWICK</span>"Prince Edrin! What a surprise. I was just taking my evening constitutional."</div> <p>She says "constitutional" the way other people say "intelligence-gathering mission."</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Lady Harwick."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HARWICK</span>"You look peaky, dear. Are you sleeping? Young men your age should be sleeping well and eating. Are you eating? I told Marta you looked thin at the autumn feast. She agreed. We both worry."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I assure you I'm "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HARWICK</span>"The Queen! Poor dear. We're all praying, of course. The temple has been full every morning I've been myself, twice. Though between us, the incense they're burning this season is atrocious. It smells like someone set fire to a perfumery. I've complained to the Head Priestess. She ignored me. Everyone ignores me. It's a burden."</div> <p>No one ignores Lady Harwick. Lady Harwick is ignored the way a thunderstorm is ignored technically possible, practically inadvisable.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HARWICK</span>"I heard the most interesting thing from Lord Veltham's wife at tea yesterday." Her voice drops to what she imagines is a whisper but is actually audible from the next hedge. "Apparently, Lord Ashborne has been entertaining ambassadors from Tormark. <em>Three</em> ambassadors. In one week. Now what do you suppose that's about?"</div> <p>My stomach tightens. Ashborne strengthening alliances. This isn't gossip it's intelligence.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I'm sure it's routine diplomacy, Lady Harwick."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HARWICK</span>"Routine diplomacy requires one ambassador, dear. Three requires ambition." She adjusts a brooch the size of a small shield. "I'm not political, of course. I leave that to the men. But a woman my age doesn't survive court this long without noticing patterns and the pattern I'm noticing is that Lord Ashborne is building something, and your mother's illness is the foundation he's building on."</div> <p>She pats my arm. Her rings dig into my sleeve.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">HARWICK</span>"Eat something, dear and sleep. You really do look peaky."</div> <p>She glides away, trailing perfume like a comet's tail. I stand in the garden and process the information she just handed me casually, between complaints about incense, wrapped in grandmotherly concern like a dagger in a silk scarf.</p> <p>Lady Harwick is the most dangerous person in this garden and she wants me to know it. I'm not sure if that's a warning or an offer of alliance.</p> <<set $d2_npc_harwick to true>> <<set $statAUT += 1>> <<set $stress += 3>> <<set $repCourt += 1>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_gardens_hub]] </div><<npcPortrait "joss" "Joss">> <h3>Scullion Joss Kitchen Gossip</h3> <p>Joss is a scullion fourteen, gap-toothed, perpetually smudged with soot, and possessed of the most efficient gossip network in Crown's Rest. He knows everything that happens in the palace because he delivers trays to every wing and nobody notices the pot-boy.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">JOSS</span>"Your Highness!" He appears at my elbow like a soot-covered apparition. "Did you hear about the merchant at the gate?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"What merchant?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">JOSS</span>"From the Free Cities. Sarrow Coast. Brought a cart full of silks silks, Your Highness, in winter! and tried to bribe Guardsman Keller to let him skip the inspection queue. Keller said no. The merchant offered double. Keller said no louder. The merchant offered triple and a bolt of Sarrow blue for his wife. Keller said his wife hates blue and arrested the merchant."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Keller's wife <em>does</em> hate blue."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">JOSS</span>"Everyone knows that except merchants from the Sarrow Coast, apparently." Joss grins. "Also don't tell Marta I told you but the wine delivery from the eastern vineyard is late, and she's furious because the banquet next week needs forty casks and she's only got thirty-two, and she says if Lord Harwick complains about the vintage again she'll put his head in the stockpot."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Would she?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">JOSS</span>"She'd try. Lord Harwick has a very large head. I'm not sure it'd fit."</div> <p>Despite everything despite the morning, the Queen, the books, the ceiling, the two-day countdown I laugh. It's a small laugh, more breath than sound, but Joss beams like he's won a tournament.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Go on, before Marta catches you gossiping."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">JOSS</span>"She already knows. She knows everything. She's like a spider in a web made of flour."</div> <p>He vanishes back into the steam. The kitchen goes on.</p> <<set $d2_npc_joss to true>> <<set $stress -= 2>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_kitchen]] </div><<npcPortrait "keller" "Guardsman Keller">> <h3>Guardsman Keller The Gate Veteran</h3> <p>Keller is sharpening his actual sword not a practice blade at the bench near the yard entrance. He's forty, weathered, with the kind of face that looks like it was carved from the same stone as the castle walls. Twenty years in the Royal Guard. He fought in the border skirmish. He has opinions about everything and shares them with the restraint of a man who has been told many times to keep his opinions to himself and has decided that advice is for other people.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">KELLER</span>"Your Highness. You sparred with the Captain this morning."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I did."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">KELLER</span>"How'd it go?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"He disarmed me twice."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">KELLER</span>"Only twice? You're improving." He tests the blade's edge with his thumb. A tiny bead of blood appears. He nods, satisfied. "I heard something interesting this morning."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"From the Sarrow Coast merchant?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">KELLER</span>"How do you never mind. No, not the merchant. From the east wing guards. They're on double rotation. The Queen's chambers are locked to all visitors except family and the Royal Healer."</div> <p>He looks at me. Keller doesn't do subtlety it's not in his skillset.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">KELLER</span>"If something's happening, the Guard should know. We can't protect what we don't understand."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Nothing's happening, Keller."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">KELLER</span>"With respect, Your Highness, when a prince says 'nothing's happening,' something is always happening. I've served three royals. I know the pattern."</div> <p>He sheathes the sword. The motion is practiced twenty years of muscle memory.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">KELLER</span>"The men are loyal, Your Highness. Whatever comes. I want you to know that."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I do know that."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">KELLER</span>"Good. Because loyalty is easier when it's acknowledged."</div> <p>He stands. Bows. Walks toward the gate, where a junior guard is struggling with the merchant's confiscated cart. Keller doesn't look back, but the message was clear: <em>we're watching, we're worried, and we're ready.</em></p> <<set $d2_npc_keller to true>> <<set $affAldric += 1>> <<set $statRES += 1>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_training_hub]] </div><h3>The Half-Written Letter</h3> <p>I pick up the letter to Rowan. Three weeks old. The ink has crusted in the nib, and when I tap it, a flake of dried black drops onto the parchment.</p> <p><em>"The court is suffocating and I'm considering taking up goat herding as an alternative career "</em></p> <p>That's where I stopped. I remember now. I was trying to be funny. Trying to write something light because Rowan's letters are always light full of tavern stories and terrible puns and sketches of people they've met on the road. A merchant with a moustache shaped like a seagull. A dog that stole a whole roast chicken from a banquet table. Small, beautiful things.</p> <p>I wanted to match that energy. I couldn't. Everything I tried to write after the goat herding line turned dark <em>Mother is worse. The court is circling. I feel like I'm standing on a trapdoor and someone's hand is on the lever.</em></p> <p>I put the letter down. If Mother is right if the Rite is the only option then this letter is a relic from a man who doesn't exist yet. A man who's still deciding.</p> <p>I fold it. Tuck it into the desk drawer.</p> <p>If I send it, it'll be the last letter Edrin ever writes.</p> <<set $d2_npc_letter to true>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_chambers_explore]] </div><h3>The Gossiping Maids</h3> <p>Two handmaidens are pressed against the wall near the tapestry of the Battle of Thornridge, speaking in the urgent whisper that palace servants use when they think they're being quiet but are absolutely not.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MAID</span>" summoned the Silverveil, I heard. Telsa saw Archsorceress Ilara crossing the bridge to the Moonspire at dawn "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MAID</span>"Ilara herself? Not one of the apprentices?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MAID</span>"Herself and the Queen's healer went to the east wing at first light. The guards doubled."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MAID</span>"Do you think she's "</div> <p>They see me. The silence is instantaneous and guilty. Both curtsy deep, formal, the kind you give when you've been caught saying something you shouldn't.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MAID</span>"Your Highness."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Ladies."</div> <p>I walk past. I feel their eyes on my back. The whispering resumes before I round the corner quieter this time, but not quiet enough.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MAID</span>" the prince looks terrible. Did you see his eyes? He hasn't been sleeping "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MAID</span>"My mum says when the Queen goes, the Ashbornes will "</div> <p>I walk faster. The palace has always been a machine that runs on gossip. Today, the gears are turning on my mother's illness, and I'm caught between the teeth.</p> <<set $d2_npc_maids to true>> <<set $stress += 2>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_corridors]] </div><<npcPortrait "marta" "Marta">> <h3>Head Cook Marta</h3> <p>The palace kitchens are a realm unto themselves a vast, low-ceilinged cavern of stone and iron where three massive hearths blaze day and night, filling the air with heat, smoke, and the complex layered aroma of twelve dishes being prepared simultaneously. Pots hang from ceiling hooks. Herbs dry in bundles above the doorways. A small army of kitchen workers junior cooks, scullions, pot-boys, pastry apprentices move in choreographed chaos that would make a military commander weep with envy.</p> <p>At the center of it all: Marta. Head Cook. Fifty-something. Built like a barrel of ale and twice as formidable. She has flour in her hair, grease on her apron, a wooden spoon in her right hand that functions as both utensil and scepter, and a voice that can be heard through two walls and a courtyard.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"OUT of my way, Joss, or I swear on the Mother's left Prince Edrin!" Her manner shifts from volcanic to warm in the time it takes her to spot me. "My boy. You ate standing up again, didn't you? I can always tell. Your breakfast tray comes back with the food gone but the chair cold."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"I prefer eating at the window."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"You prefer <em>not sitting still long enough for your thoughts to catch up.</em> It's the same thing, and I've been watching you do it since you were nine." She steers me toward a stool near the prep table with the gentle inevitability of a river current. "Sit. Eat. I've got fresh pastries coming out cheese and herb, the ones you like."</div> <p>I sit. Resistance is theoretical when Marta is involved.</p> <p>She puts a plate in front of me two pastries, golden-brown, steam curling from the latticed top, the smell of melted cheese and rosemary sharp enough to cut through every other scent in the kitchen. They're absurdly good. Marta has been making these since I was a child, and the recipe has not changed because perfection does not require revision.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"You look thin," she says, which is her standard opening regardless of my actual weight.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"You always say that."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"You're always thin. Eat."</div> <p>She watches me bite into the pastry. Her expression settles into satisfaction the particular look of a cook watching someone enjoy their food, which is the closest thing to religious ecstasy that exists in the culinary profession.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Marta. Have you heard anything... unusual today? About the east wing?"</div> <p>Her hands, which were wiping the prep table, slow. She doesn't look up.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"I hear everything in this kitchen, Your Highness. Sound travels through stone. The scullions hear the guards, the guards hear the ministers, the ministers hear the Queen, and all of it ends up in my kitchen before the soup is cold."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"So what?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"I've been making cheese pastries since dawn. You know what that means."</div> <p>I do. Marta makes cheese pastries when the palace is scared. She made them the day my father died. She made them during the border skirmish. She made them when the plague hit the lower city three years ago.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"Your mother is the strongest woman I've ever known," Marta says quietly, her back to me, stirring something that doesn't need stirring. "Whatever she's asked of you she wouldn't ask if there were another way."</div> <p>I look at her. She looks at the pot. Neither of us says anything else. The kitchen goes on around us the clatter of pots, the shout of orders, the sizzle of fat in pans. The world is ending and the pastries are perfect and Marta is stirring a pot and somewhere in this equation is a truth about how life continues even when it shouldn't.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Thank you, Marta."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">MARTA</span>"Eat the second one. You're thin."</div> <<set $d2_npc_marta to true>> <<set $energy += 10>> <<set $stress -= 5>> <<set $repStaff += 1>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_kitchen]] </div><<npcPortrait "perrin" "Perrin">> <h3>The Night Guard Perrin</h3> <p>I open the door to get air the room is warm from the rebuilt fire and I can't breathe and nearly walk into the night guard. Perrin. Young. Earnest. The kind of guard who takes the night shift seriously, which means he stands at rigid attention for eight hours even though no one is watching.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">PERRIN</span>"Your Highness! I do you need anything?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"No. Just air."</div> <p>He nods. Stands aside. I lean against the doorframe and breathe the corridor air cooler, stone-scented, with a faint draft from the stairwell.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Quiet night," I say, because the alternative is going back inside and staring at the ceiling.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">PERRIN</span>"Yes, Your Highness. Very quiet." He hesitates. "Except there was something. Around midnight. Music. From the guest wing."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"That's Rowan. A friend."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">PERRIN</span>"Ah. Good music. Sad, though."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Yes."</div> <p>We stand in comfortable silence for a moment. Perrin is perhaps the least complicated person I've interacted with today a guard on a post, doing his job, noticing music in the dark. There's something restful about simplicity.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Perrin. Have you ever had to make a choice you didn't want to make?"</div> <p>He thinks about it. Actually thinks, which I appreciate I'm so tired of reflexive answers and political calculations.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">PERRIN</span>"When I joined the Guard, Your Highness. My father wanted me to take over the tannery. Leather trade. Good money. Stable life. But I wanted I needed something else. I couldn't explain it. I just knew the tannery wasn't... me. So I left. My father didn't speak to me for two years."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Now?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">PERRIN</span>"Now he brags to his friends that his son guards the prince." A small smile. "He came around. It took time, but he came around."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"What if the choice is bigger than a tannery?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">PERRIN</span>"Then I suppose the coming-around takes longer. But in my experience, Your Highness, the people who love you don't stop. They just need time to understand the new shape of things."</div> <p>The new shape of things. I file that beside <em>vaelthin</em> and <em>one who has walked between</em> and <em>the same rose in a new body</em> and all the other phrases that are collecting in my chest like stones in a cairn.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Good night, Perrin."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">PERRIN</span>"Good night, Your Highness."</div> <p>I close the door. The ceiling is waiting.</p> <<set $d2_npc_perrin to true>> <<set $statRES += 1>> <<set $stress -= 2>> <<completeObjective "speak_perrin">> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_chambers_explore]] </div><<npcPortrait "tamsin" "Tamsin">> <h3>Young Recruit Tamsin</h3> <p>A young woman recruit, by the uniform, which is too clean and too well-pressed to belong to anyone who's seen real duty is methodically destroying a training dummy with a quarterstaff. Her form is wrong. Her grip is wrong. Her footwork is wrong. But the intensity is right. She's hitting the dummy like it said something about her mother.</p> <p>She sees me and freezes. The quarterstaff clatters against the dummy's wooden head one final time, a dying echo.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">TAMSIN</span>"Y-Your Highness. I didn't I wasn't expecting "</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"At ease, recruit." I pick up the quarterstaff she's dropped. "You're overextending on your backswing. You're opening up your left side every time you commit to a high strike."</div> <p>She blinks.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">TAMSIN</span>"You... know quarterstaff?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Aldric made me learn every weapon in the yard before he let me specialise. His philosophy is that a swordsman who doesn't understand a spear doesn't understand reach, and a man who doesn't understand reach doesn't understand combat."</div> <p>I demonstrate the correction shorter backswing, elbow tucked, weight on the balls of the feet rather than the heels. She watches with the focused intensity of someone who has been teaching herself from observation and is hearing actual instruction for the first time.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">TAMSIN</span>"Tamsin, Your Highness. From the northern garrison. I transferred three weeks ago."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Three weeks and nobody's corrected your form?"</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">TAMSIN</span>"The senior guards say recruits learn by doing and by getting hit."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"That's half right. You learn by getting hit <em>after</em> someone explains what you're doing wrong. Otherwise you just learn how to get hit."</div> <p>I work with her for ten minutes. It's the first time today that my mind has been fully in my body not in the Queen's chambers, not in the library, not circling the drain of the Rite. Just here. Hands on a staff. Feet on stone. The simple physics of force and leverage.</p> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">TAMSIN</span>"Thank you, Your Highness." Tamsin's form is marginally better. Marginally is a start.</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">EDRIN</span>"Practice the short backswing. Fifty repetitions, morning and night. You'll feel the difference in a week."</div> <div class="dialogue"><span class="speaker">TAMSIN</span>"Yes, Your Highness."</div> <p>I set the staff down. The brief clarity is already fading, the dread seeping back in like water through cracks. But for ten minutes, I was just a man who knew something useful and shared it.</p> <<set $d2_npc_tamsin to true>> <<set $statPRO += 1>> <<set $stress -= 3>> <<set $repMilitary += 1>> <div class="scene-end"> [[Continue → |day-2_training_hub]] </div><<npcPortrait "vaelin" "Brother Vaelin">> <h3>The Theology Student Brother Vaelin</h3> <p>A young man in temple robes is sitting cross-legged on the floor between the theology shelves, surrounded by a fortress of open books and looking like he hasn't moved in several hours.
